pool.titulo: La Casa Torcida de Lavenham: el hogar de 600 años que sus dueños han convertido en una atracción turística premiada
pool.resumen:
Dudo mucho que en algún momento te hayas perdido tanto por Inglaterra como para llegar al pueblo inglés de Lavenham , en Suffolk, pero tampoco sería descabellado teniendo en cuenta que una de sus casas se ha convertido en toda una atracción turística. De entre todos los edificios medievales que han aguantado el paso del tiempo, esta casa de 1935 es, de lejos, la más llamativa.
Lleva más de 600 años aguantando las inclemencias del tiempo y el propio paso de este último mientras sus vigas y ventanas completamente torcidas se convertían en espectáculo. Si al verla te preguntas cómo demonios sigue eso en pie después de todo este tiempo, toca reconocer que sus dueños tienen parte de culpa de que siga así.
La crisis que salvó las casas de Lavenham La conocida como Crooked House nace de un rico comerciante de lana que la mandó construir en el pueblo, pero lo hizo con más prisas que cuidado. Como las vigas de madera no se habían secado lo suficiente, al perder la humedad se empezaron a retorcer por el peso hasta deformar la estructura de la casa y quedar tal y como está hoy.

pool.titulo: Científicos españoles proponen recuperar el mar de Aral para evitar la emisión de cientos de millones de toneladas de CO₂
pool.resumen:
Las imágenes satelitales no dejan lugar a dudas, lo que en los años 60 era el cuarto lago más grande del mundo se ha convertido hoy en un cementerio de barcos en medio del desierto. El desastre del mar de Aral , provocado cuando a la Unión Soviética se le metió entre ceja y ceja convertir toda la región en una potencia mundial del algodón, se ha convertido en obsesión para el Centro de Estudios Avanzados de Blanes y el Instituto Catalán de Investigación del Agua .
Y hacen bien, porque estudiar lo ocurrido en ese desastre natural que se llevó por delante 68.000 kilómetros cuadrados de superficie, puede ayudarnos a entender por qué esa catástrofe sigue pasándonos factura. Lo que les preocupa, especialmente, no es cómo su industria de la pesca se fue al garete o las tormentas de polvo que se siguen generando, sino el carbono que había quedado atrapado bajo el agua.

pool.titulo: The Best LEGO Gifts to Buy For Adults in 2026
pool.resumen: Looking for a gift for the adult LEGO builder in your life? Look no further – we've gathered all the best sets this year.
pool.contenido:
There has never been a better time to be a LEGO Adult, which means there has never been a better time to be someone looking for a gift for a LEGO Adult—even if that adult LEGO fan is you.
In 2026, LEGO has released hundreds of new sets globally, across dozens of different themes. Some of the most popular adult collector lines include Icons, Botanical, Art, and Architecture, but it’s the licensed entertainment lines that tend to get us the most excited at IGN. LEGO has teamed up with some of pop culture’s biggest brands to bring nerds story-driven builds in the worlds of Lord of the Rings, Harry Potter, Pokémon, and more.
As we head into the holiday season, we’ve compiled a list of must-have sets for LEGO Adults. Most of these sets were released in 2026, and have been amongst the best-reviewed builds of the year. We’ve prioritized recommending LEGO Adult sets at different price points, so if the recommended set is above (or below) your budget, be sure to read the description for another suggestion within that franchise.
Best LEGO Gift Ideas for Adults Here’s a look at every set in the article. Click on any that look good to you, or keep on reading to find out more info about each set.
The Lord of the Rings Minas Tirith LEGO Set At 8,278 pieces, Minas Tirith is the largest Lord of the Rings build released yet. LEGO Model Designers employed a hybrid-scale model to recreate the grandeur of the Gondor capital. The exterior of the city uses minifig-scale, microscale, and nanoscale to create a forced perspective effect—similar to the strategy Peter Jackson employed to represent different sized Lord of the Rings characters from mostly similarly sized human actors on the big screen. The detailed build comes with 10 minifigs, in case you need to stage The Battle of Pelennor Fields.
If this massive Lord of the Rings set is too expensive or just plain too big for your giftee, consider the Sauron Helmet set , a 538-piece build that makes for an intimidating office display.
PlayStation LEGO Set Following the success of brick-build recreations of class game consoles like NES (retired), Atari 2600 (retired), and SEGA Genesis , LEGO has released a near 1:1 scale LEGO model of PlayStation . At 1,911 pieces, the retro build includes two interior dioramas inspired by classic games, making it a fun display piece.
If the PlayStation set is a little out of your price range, the 421-piece Game Boy build offers a smaller set that taps into the same sense of gaming nostalgia. Check out our thoughts on the build and our interview with the LEGO designer .
Pokémon Eevee LEGO Set Ever since LEGO’s Pokémon licensing deal was announced in 2025, fans have been gearing up to catch them all. This past year was the big LEGO Pokémon launch, and the star of the show was arguably Eevee . The small, 587-piece build punches above its weight. LEGO Model Designers really nailed the cuteness of Eevee’s design, from the big eyes to the posable ears to the bushy tail, making it a good display piece once finished.
For gift-givers looking to spend a bit more on the Pokémon fan in their life, the 6,838-piece Venusaur, Charizard, and Blastoise set gives you three Kanto Region Evolutions for one display.
Project Hail Mary LEGO Set For all the readers (and the film adaptation watchers) out there, LEGO released a microscale replica of the interstellar spacecraft from Project Hail Mary . What makes this 830-piece build so rewarding is the functionality of the finished product; by rotating the crank, the spaceship shifts from flight mode to centrifuge mode. It looks super cool, and elevates a cool LEGO display for an office or den into an interactive adventure. If the LEGO readers in your life aren’t sci-fi fans, try gifting them one of the toy company’s book nooks . These builds are designed to nestle cozily between volumes on a bookshelf. While most are based on specific books, such as the Harry Potter-themed Dumbledore’s Office , the latest release is a Bookstore: Book Nook . The two-story (no pun intended) bookstore setting, complete with spiral staircase and plenty of tomes, works for readers of any genre.
Zelda: Ocarina of Time - The Final Battle LEGO Set Nintendo’s 2026 remake of the legendary Nintendo 64 game Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched in November, and quickly became one of the best-selling games of the year. LEGO’s Ocarina of Time - The Final Battle set commemorates this important game milestone by depicting the climactic showdown between Link, Zelda, and Navi and final boss beast Ganon. Our reviewer Seth G. Macy particularly loved minifig Ganondorf’s cape, the build’s lever mechanism, and the designers’ choice to go print over decal. There are plenty of Nintendo LEGO sets for fans to enjoy; we also recommend the Mario Kart - Luigi & Mach 8 set , a sibling follow-up to Mario & Standard Kart .
LEGO Iron Man Mark 3 Collectors’ Edition LEGO Set If you have any friends who still haven’t recovered from the “I love you 3000” days of the MCU, get them the Iron Man Mark 3 Collectors’ Edition set . With 1,297 total pieces, builders can lovingly recreate the iconic suit from the Infinity Saga, and then display the figure for eternity. If the Marvel fans in your life skew more sinister and have less time on their hands, we recommend the 413-piece Venom Bust set , complete with searching (and removable) tongue.
LEGO Star Wars Boba Fett LEGO Set LEGO and Star Wars go together like blue milk and ronto wraps, which makes the Star Wars LEGO line particularly robust. One of the latest, greatest builds include a 1,544-piece Boba Fett set (the Fett set, for short) that would look good on any bookshelf. If you’ve got the budget to burn, we also recommend the 1,809-piece Mandalorian N-1 Starfighter set or the Executor Super Star Destroyer —a massive, 6,130-piece set that is 4.5 feet long once assembled.

pool.titulo: Rockstar no estará contenta. El hacker que filtró GTA 6 se marcha a casa con un "no lo vuelvas a hacer"
pool.resumen:
Aunque GTA 6 ya está a un clic de nosotros, cuesta olvidar uno de los momentos más delicados que vivió Rockstar durante el desarrollo del juego. Allá por septiembre de 2022, con cuatro años aún por delante para la llegada del juego, la compañía fue víctima de un ataque informático que acabó con decenas de vídeos de su esperadísimo mundo abierto circulando por internet. El primero de los dos grandes hackeos a la empresa se saldó con Arion Kurtaj , el hacker responsable del ataque a Rockstar , internado en un hospital psiquiátrico de alta seguridad. Ahora, tras haberse declarado culpable de los hechos, ha sido puesto en libertad .
La trayectoria delictiva de Kurtaj, miembro del grupo internacional de hackers Lapsus$, no fue precisamente insignificante. Entre 2021 y 2022, participó en ataques contra Uber, el banco digital Revolut y la operadora de telecomunicaciones BT/EE . Tras atacar a Rockstar y ser pillado con las manos en la masa, en 2023 un juez determinó que el joven británico seguía obsesionado con el hacking y que, debido a sus habilidades informáticas, representaba un "alto riesgo de causar daños graves a la sociedad". pool.titulo: Arnold Schwarzenegger elige su película de ciencia ficción con robots favorita, y no es Terminator: "No será la más conocida, pero su impacto fue profundo en mí"
pool.resumen:
Desde su debut, Arnold Schwarzenegger puede presumir de haber salido en más de medio centenar de películas , tres de ellas dirigidas por James Cameron . El canadiense le dio el personaje que, junto a Conan el Bárbaro , le convirtió en una gran estrella de Hollywood. Y debemos admitir que The Terminator y, más aún, su secuela estrenada diez años después fueron filmes impresionantes. Pero ninguna de estas dos es la cinta de ciencia ficción sobre robots favorita del actor.
En lugar de tirar de ego, como cuando compartió cuál era, en su opinión, la peor película de la saga Terminator , el también político americano quiso revelar hace unos años una lista con seis títulos imprescindibles para él. Ninguno contaba con su participación delante de las cámaras, aunque uno de ellos sí llevaba la firma de James Cameron. La selección incluía clásicos como E.T., el extraterrestre (1982) , El padrino (1972), Sonrisas y lágrimas (1965), Titanic (1997), Sin perdón (1992) y Westword: Almas de metal (1973), que quizás te suene más por su reboot como serie de televisión estrenada por HBO en 2016. pool.titulo: Compraron por 6.500 libras un barco de la Segunda Guerra Mundial en eBay y descubrieron que había sido clave en el desembarco de Normandía
pool.resumen:
Durante la pandemia nos dio por hacer cosas de lo más extrañas. Hubo gente a la que le dio por hacer pan, a otros por jugar a Animal Crossing , estaban los que hacían carreras por el balcón, y a Simon y Gemma Robins el venazo les llevó a comprar un barco de madera en eBay de casi 22 metros de eslora para restaurarlo. No juzgamos.
El caso es que, pese a la rareza, en realidad sabían qué estaban haciendo. Ya estaban acostumbrados a restaurar embarcaciones más pequeñas y convertir furgonetas en caravanas, así que cuando vieron aquel viejo barco llamado Sarinda corriendo el riesgo de ser completamente desguazado, sabían que debían restaurarlo para evitarlo.
De la Segunda Guerra Mundial a YouTube La clave estaba en que el Sarinda no era un barco cualquiera . Para entender toda la historia toca saltar hasta diciembre de 1943, cuando salió de los astilleros de Berthon bajo el nombre de ML 1392 y, apenas seis meses después, se convirtió en uno de los barcos que ayudaron a las tropas aliadas a realizar el desembarco de Normandía .
Tras guiar a los barcos de los aliados para esquivar las minas y sobrevivir a la Segunda Guerra Mundial , el barco sirvió para llevar turistas de paseo por Liverp

pool.titulo: Nintendo Switch Online Just Got a Long-Awaited Update, Alongside Another GameCube Classic
pool.resumen: GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature.
pool.contenido:
GameCube launch title Wave Race: Blue Storm is now available via the Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack service, alongside a long-awaited new feature.
If you're an Expansion Pack subscriber, you can now update your Nintendo Classics GameCube app to gain access to the cult classic aquatic racer — and also unlock the ability to remove the app's annoying border graphics.
The Nintendo Classic apps have a border gradient that until now you couldn't remove — and it's something that's proven a bugbear from fans who want a cleaner look. For now, only the GameCube app has the option to simply have clear black borders instead, though it seems likely the other console apps will follow. Or, maybe this is something only the technical power of Switch 2 can pull off?
"Storm warning! Prepare to ride the waves!" reads an official blurb for the game. "Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube system in 2001. Compete in contests of speed and technique—either racing against your rivals or going up against your own records. As you race across the waves, you can see the skies changes from calm and sunny to surging storms... Weather conditions can affect visibility, water levels, and the height of the waves over the course of a race, so you'll need to be prepared for whatever comes!"
Wave Race: Blue Storm becomes the 12th GameCube title available on Switch 2 via the Expansion Pack subscription service, following the previous additions of Chibi-Robo!, F-Zero GX, Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance, Luigi's Mansion, Super Mario Strikers, Pokémon XD: Gale of Darkness, SoulCalibur 2, Star Fox Adventures, Super Mario Sunshine, The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker and Wario World.

pool.titulo: Steam revamps its marketplace for the 2nd time this year
pool.resumen: Big news for the skin barons in your life.
pool.contenido:
If you're normal, you probably never think about the Steam community market. If you're like me, you only touch it to sell the mountains of trading cards you get from idling . If you're a true lunatic, you're running a roaring trade in Counter-Strike 2 skins and are either unfathomably rich or trapped in a life of penury.
Either way, some news: Valve has been tinkering at the Steam marketplace again, and in an update yesterday announced a rebuilt market home page that's slightly more pleasant to handle and look at, while being more personalised to the games you're actually playing. This is in addition to a set of changes to the market Valve released (in beta) back in May .
The new market home is, says Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint. It's swapped out the pre-update Popular Items section—which mostly just showed a list of CS2 crates—for new Trending Items lists that show the popular market items for games you've actually been playing. When I look at it, I see Path of Exile, Warframe, Crisis In The Kremlin, and, uh, Dota 2. I've never touched Dota 2 in my life, so not sure what's happening there, but you get the idea.
You've also now got a watchlist that will let you keep track of various market items across multiple games. You can save specific items, a general item type, or even a particular search. I imagine this will be useful to those of you who play the Steam market like an '80s Wall Street guy shouting into a big phone.
The biggest change for me personally—that's why people read the news, for the biggest changes for me personally—is streamlined selling and relisting. You can now change the price of items you have listed for sale without laboriously taking them down and relisting them. You can just update the price tag and have done with it. Similarly, if you're selling directly from the Steam mobile app, you'll be able to approve those sales via a pop-up rather than navigating to the confirmation page. This is truly huge news for the weirdest guys you know (me).
All that aside, the market home page will now also track your in-progress badges, and search results now have a list view. There are a few more new things, but Valve confined them to an 'and finally' set of bulletpoints, so here they are in their original bulletpoint form.
My Listings and History are now on a dedicated page, with a summary on the Market Home page "Trending", or items that are newly popular, is now a sort option for results and buy/sell listings Updated Sell Dialog with the newer graphs, with improved usability on mobile devices Counter-Strike 2 containers show and link to their possible contents Sort by Popularity and Sort by Price return better results, faster All Market pages load faster and are more responsive 2026 games : All the upcoming games

pool.titulo: GTA 6 Players Are Optimizing the Money Glitch to Within an Inch of Its Life to Make $100,000 in Just 10 Minutes
pool.resumen: We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6, but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.
pool.contenido:
We’ve already covered players using infinite money glitches to get rich quickly in GTA 6 , but people are taking it to the next level. New money-making optimization strategies are seeing players become millionaires in a couple of hours, while still in the early game.
Instead of playing the game as intended and robbing stores, banks, and gang hideouts, some GTA 6 players are repeating the same actions over and over to generate money fast.
How to do the new GTA 6 money glitch The new method sees players using vans and character swaps at a location in a town called Hamlet. In Hamlet, there’s an industrial area with a big warehouse outside of town, with a teddy bear van parked outside.
There are drugs inside the van outside as well as inside the warehouse itself. To do the glitch, you need to register two vans, turn up to the location, and have your partner call in a different personal vehicle while the player calls in one of the personal vans and takes the loot.
Stow the loot in the back of your personal vehicle, then drive the teddy van parked outside into the warehouse, parking it inside, on the right of the door, at which point tell your partner to wait in the car. The player then gets out and drives the teddy bear van parked inside (both of these vans are empty of loot at this point) and park this opposite the other van, so both vans have their back doors facing the shutter entrance.
Next, switch to your partner and exit the first teddy van before heading outside, where you switch back. Then ask your partner to drive the personal van loaded with all the loot. Using the partner menu, ask your partner to fence the loot, and watch them drive off to do so.
Once your partner has driven off, use the Scooter Bros app to call in the second personal van. After backing the van up to the warehouse, switch to the partner fencing the loot, before immediately switching back. This respawns both teddy bear vans and the loot inside, but it also keeps the two you moved earlier where you parked them inside and fills them with loot, essentially doubling the take.
According to one GTA 6 player who posted about this new method on Reddit , the technique earns you between $88,000-$100,000 in under 10 minutes.
Some of the replies to the Reddit post asked the OP when their in-game bank account limit will be raised, suggesting they’re still relatively early in the game. Later on, more lucrative robbery opportunities open up for players anyway, and you can pull off $100k jobs with way less hassle than this, and while having some actual fun whilst you’re at it.
The question is whether Rockstar patches early days money glitches like these out of GTA 6. GTA 6's first post-launch patch failed to take action, but I imagine it won't be long before Rockstar does something about this.

pool.titulo: I Watched GTA 6's In-Game TV Shows For Hours, They're Absolutely Wild
pool.resumen: Rockstar's satire has reached new levels with in-game cartoons like Barnyard Blue and the dark comedy The Tyrone Show.
pool.contenido:
Of all the things I expected of Grand Theft Auto 6, sitting there watching in-game TV for like…two hours was not on my list. Freshly pre-loaded and ready to go on my Xbox Series X right at 3am on the west coast, claiming to be in New Zealand, booting it up for the first time had me rubbing my hands like Birdman – I was ready to get in the thick of it in GTA 6. What could this new Vice City's criminal underworld make me do? Not much. Will I have to survive shootouts early on, and will I need to contend with the new wanted system in a car chase? Not really. Mostly because as soon as I got to Jason's home in the opening hour, I sat my ass down on his living room couch, flipped on Weazel News and couldn't believe what I was seeing.
In GTA 6, you can sit on the couch and flip through three TV channels of original in-universe programming – full on TV shows made for the game, existing within the fiction of its world. You have Weazel News, the nutty right-wing parody that broadcasts news segments and TV series with the production value of something we'd see in our real world. Then there's the Telemundo spoof called Megamundo that shows Spanish-language soap operas / telenovelas, but with the absurdity cranked up several notches. Lastly, there's the Visit Leonida channel that's dedicated to advertising tourist attractions and businesses across this fictional rendition of Florida, satirizing modern economics and business.
And no, these are not channels with maybe a couple minutes' worth of gags to see once and move on from – these act as legit television programming, shows with multiple episodes that go on for six to eight minutes each. Why would I flip through my free Roku channels or be hit with choice paralysis on my own TV's built-in streaming apps when GTA 6 could rapid fire some of the wildest shit the series has done with shows you'd never see on real TV?
I'd get a kick out of Alan Wake 2's Koskela Brothers commercials or Max Payne's Adventures of Captain Baseball Bat Boy episodes, which aligned with Remedy's style and universe. pool.titulo: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 Teaser Pretty Much Confirms Fifth Playable Faction — and the Appearance of a Would-Be Chaos God
pool.resumen: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.
pool.contenido:
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 is almost upon us, and publisher Plaion has released a new trailer that teases the appearance of a fan-favorite character from the tabletop game — and even the fifth playable faction.
Dawn of War 4, developed by King Art Games, launches with four playable races: the Space Marines; Orks, Necrons, and the Adeptus Mechanicus. We knew that the developer had plans to release more factions over time, as has been the case with previous entries in the real-time strategy series. But we didn’t know which would come first… until now.
Warning! Potential spoilers for Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 follow.
The teaser ends with a tease for Dawn of War 4’s first DLC faction. We see the unmistakable eyes of Vashtorr the Arkifane, alongside the narration: “And what began on Aurelia is coming to Kronus.”
That’s a clear reference to Chaos as the new faction, given Aurelia, the former homeworld and capital of the Blood Ravens Space Marine Chapter, was gobbled up by the Warp (Warhammer 40,000’s version of a hell dimension full of demons), before it was spat out and besieged by Black Legion Chaos Space Marines. So, it would make sense that Chaos Space Marines are the new faction. Will we see further corruption of the Blood Ravens play out?
Who is Vashtorr the Arkifane? But what about Vashtorr the Arkifane? Vashtorr is a sort of in-between, Chaos Undivided being who appears to have designs on becoming the fifth Chaos god. According to the lore, Vashtorr came into existence within the Warp due to our obsessive pursuit of tech innovation (feels pretty relatable right now, doesn’t it?). As such, Vashtorr acts as a sort of arms dealer to the existing Chaos factions, creating powerful daemon weapons and engines for use in war.
Ever since Vashtorr’s dramatic introduction into the Warhammer 40,000 universe with the Arks of Omen storyline a few years ago, and his uneasy alliance with Horus’ successor, Abaddon the Despoiler, fans have wondered about his masterplan. As is Games Workshop’s want, the overarching Warhammer 40,000 storyline moves slowly, so we don’t really have much to go on beyond he’s big, he’s mean, and he wants it all. Perhaps Dawn of War 4 will shed more light on his motivations?
Either way, it would be really cool if we got to actually command Vashtorr on the battlefield, although you’d expect him to be incredibly overpowered, given what we know of his power set from the lore. Dawn of War 4 is the first Warhammer 40,000 video game to feature a playable Primarch (one of the Emperor’s ultra powerful sons). Could we see Lion El'Jonson go up against Vashtorr in the DLC? That would be quite something.
It’s not long before we find out. Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 launches on PC on December 3, 2026.

pool.titulo: 'Maybe It's Time': Sebastian Stan Fuels Fears Over Bucky's Fate in Avengers: Doomsday
pool.resumen: Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time."
pool.contenido:
Sebastian Stan has fueled MCU fan fears that Bucky Barnes could meet his end in Avengers: Doomsday after dropping a cryptic comment that "maybe it's time."
With the massive crossover movie set to hit theaters next month, Stan was recently asked about Bucky's long-term future in the Marvel Cinematic Universe — and his response did little to calm nervous fans.
Having debuted all the way back in 2011's Captain America: The First Avenger, Bucky is one of the last remaining Phase One veterans still standing on the front lines. Now, with his old pal Steve Rogers back front and center for this next installment , many fans have long suspected Bucky's 15-year arc could be about to culminate with a long-awaited reunion followed by a tragic end.
"I'm always happy to keep playing him," Stan said, while appearing recently on the Next Best Picture podcast. "I don't know if the decision's up to me, ultimately.
"I'm ready to take the character in all kinds of different ways," he continued, "but I can't make that decision, it's the powers that be. And I think they have a lot going on, they have a lot on their plate. Do I feel we've explored that character, there's nowhere else to go, I think we did our best? I do think we've done our best so far."
To be fair to Stan, after appearances in nine films and his own Disney+ spinoff, it's hard to know exactly where the character can continue to evolve. He is arguably the most experienced member of the New Avengers team, but this is a role that could also be provided by Yelena Belova. He has long since redeemed himself for his days as the Winter Soldier. And with Steve's story (presumably) wrapped up again with these latest Avengers movies, it's unclear what else there is for Bucky to do.
Stan has attempted to pitch a Bucky solo project to Marvel in the past — a thriller movie in the same vein as Denis Villeneuve-directed thriller Sicario — but noted again here that he had only received a non-commital response from MCU boss Kevin Feige.
"I don't think that that character totally got to fully live out his arc in the way that he has in the comics for instance, or that I've wanted," Stan concluded. "I'm always ready, but we're at that point now where I can feel it, he needs to either evolve somewhere, or maybe it's time. It's one of those."
Yikes.
While Bucky is beloved by MCU fans, Doomsday's apparent focus on the returning Steve Rogers provides a potentially unique narrative oppurtunity for the two characters' time-travelling bromance to reach an emotional conclusion. Will Bucky repay Steve for saving him by sacrificing his own life? Or will Doom simply kill him to upset Steve? Regardless of what happens, it's worth recalling something Chris Evans said recently of his character's own "brutal" arc in Doomsday :
"The Russos love beating up Steve Rogers," Evans remarked. "Their favourite thing to do is to just beat the crap out of him. To them that's what makes a hero, and that's someone who gets punched so many times but still gets up. So they keep finding new ways to kick his butt but this one was brutal, and a really good examination into his nature and his values."
What better way to knock Steve down than for Doom to kill Cap's original wingman? (And perhaps we should also be worried for Steve's son too, especially as the suggestion is that Doom is seeking revenge for the loss of his own loved ones .)
Of course, nothing yet is certain — and next year's Avengers: Secret Wars is expected to provide something of another MCU reset, meaning any death in Doomsday may not necessarily prove permanent. Still, thinking back to Avengers: Endgame, a few of its biggest deaths have been left as-is so as to not undermine their impact — something a tragic fate for Bucky would likely also qualify for.
The fate of the multiverse — and one James Buchanan "Bucky" Barnes — will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday opens in theaters on December 18.
Image credit: Marvel.

pool.titulo: Mass Effect Universe Would Have Answered Trilogy Ending Questions and Squadmate Fates, Writer Says
pool.resumen: BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates.
pool.contenido:
BioWare's canceled Mass Effect Universe would have addressed Mass Effect 3's controversial endings and the fates of Shepard's squadmates, one of the game's writers has said.
For more than a decade, Mass Effect fans have debated how BioWare could reconcile the wildly divergent endings of Mass Effect 3 — and satisfy players who insisted that their particular ending choice should be canon (I see you, Destroy fans). But according to one of the writers behind the now-canceled Mass Effect Universe, the studio had actually cracked the puzzle before EA scrapped the project and closed BioWare forever.
Speaking during a reddit fan Q&A supporting the "Save Mass Effect" fan movement, Mass Effect: Annihilation novel author Cat Valente — who spent three years on the writing team for the unfinished sequel — offered a bittersweet glimpse into how the narrative team approached the franchise's biggest lingering questions.
While strict NDAs signed with published EA continue to prevent Valente from revealing specific plot details, she emphasized that reconciling Mass Effect 3's endings was front and center for the game's writers room, and noted that the team wasn't relying on a single silver bullet to bridge the 600-year narrative gap between the original trilogy and this upcoming fifth installment.
"[We] worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn't make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel," Valente wrote.
"Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall f***ing order*. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be *really hard.* An elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn't take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible... it takes a long time, and it's not obvious how best to pull it off when you're the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing.
"And it's become really clear that it's impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices. We burned out so many valuable neurons going up against that problem. I know so many people think it's easy, just make Destroy canon and move on, but consider that, for example, I feel as strongly about Synthesis as others do about Destroy. And everyone feels strongly about choices mattering. Do you really think there is a single solution that would have satisfied everyone? In a *video game*?
"But we did our best, and I think we landed in a good place," she concluded. "There wasn't one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can't say any more than that."
As a hugely knowledgeable fan of the original trilogy — enough that she got the gig writing Andromeda's quarian ark prequel novel — Valente emphasized that the fates of the trilogy's loyal squadmates had also been a key consideration for the Mass Effect Universe team.
"You would have been able to know everything you wanted to know about them," she said, when asked for her own thoughts of what characters such as Garrus, Tali and Wrex did next. "I don't have headcanons about those fates, I have canon-canons. I know you'd have been able to find out about them because one of my jobs was to write all those fates and their possible variations (all then submitted to the room, workshopped with everyone, and sent to higher-ups for approval...)
"God, it was like being asked to stitch a nice border on the Shroud of Turin," she continued. "I put on my Big Writer Pants for that one and gave it every bit of talent I have, because I love those characters beyond measure, and they more than earned my best."
Of course, we know that Universe would have seen at least one fan-favorite character return: Liara, now 600 years older — around middle age for a long-lived asari. But what about others? Asked for specifics, Valente noted her NDA blocked her from confirming specific names, but that there had been widespread discussion of bringing back every character possible.
"I think the best way to answer your question is to say that any character who physically *could* survive, we considered allowing to survive into the new game and made decisions on them," Valente teased. "We thought about all the things you'd have wanted us to think about, and I hope you do believe that, because it's the truth. Everyone in that room loved those characters, or loved to hate them, as much as any fan. We took each and every one of them and their fates very seriously."
So, who could have survived? Alongside the asari, the krogan are another long-lived Mass Effect species — and some fans believe we already got a glimpse at an older Grunt in the krogan civil war artwork released by BioWare a couple of years ago. Could Wrex also still be around? While he'd be ancient, it would not be impossible. Synthetic characters like EDI could certainly be around (and even if you'd picked Destroy, could surely have been rebooted eventually from a backup).
And then there are the characters and plotlines from Andromeda — a game that's nowhere near as beloved as the original Mass Effect trilogy, but whose storyline was still expected to factor into Universe in some way. Indeed, Valente revealed, Andromeda fans would have finally gained the answer to some of the spinoffs lingering questions (which were originally set to be answered in long-scrapped Andromeda sequels). pool.contenido:
GTA 6 actor Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online.
Warning! Spoilers for Mandy's role in GTA 6 follow.
Lexie Shoaibi did performance capture and voice over for Mandy, a woman you meet early on in the game. Mandy asks Jason to fix a clogged sink in her house, but comes out in a tiny bikini once he’s under the sink with a wrench. It didn't take long for the internet to latch on to Mandy, with countless social media posts discussing the character.
Shoaibi appeared on a Hasan Piker stream a few days ago, chatting about GTA 6 while raising money for charity. During the stream, she spoke about the newfound fame and reaction to her character.
“I don’t know how that happened,” Shoaibi said. “People pretending to be me? It’s thrilling. Please stop, but it’s also so exciting. It’s sort of bittersweet.”
Shoaibi hinted at this issue in a seperate Instagram post in which she warned her followers about fake accounts from people trying to impersonate her on social media. Referring to one X / Twitter account that has popped up in the last week purporting to be her own, she said: "This is fake! I don’t have a Twitter! This isn’t me! Please, someone, make it go away, ew!”
Meanwhile, Shoaibi revealed she spent around 10 days on set playing Mandy, but she also did a few other NPC voices while working with Rockstar.
Warning! Specific Mandy spoilers follow.
Despite Mandy only being a minor character in Chapter 1, Rockstar’s attention to detail put a bit of a spotlight on the character. As well as her basically being nude, the garden outside Mandy’s house hides a dark secret . When Jason is fixing the sink, he finds something clogged in it. You might think it’s a chicken bone, but closer inspection shows it’s a severed human finger. Check the trunk of Mandy’s car and you can find a kill kit. Have a nosey around her back garden and you’ll find vats of acid and a freshly dug grave. The game basically hints that she’s not a harmless stalker — she’s a serial killer. No, you can’t “fix her.”
“She’s a lot of fun, so if you play the game, let me know if you find me,” Shoaibi said in another statement about her character before people made it weird. “Y’all there aren’t words!!!! Thank you so much for the love and support. This is crazy!! Ily forever!”

pool.titulo: Why is GTA 6 Getting Review Bombed?
pool.resumen: Why GTA 6 user reviews are so low: Metacritic review-bombing explained.
pool.contenido:
GTA 6 tied with the original version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-scored game in history based on Metacritic ratings, sitting pretty at a 99 critic score. Rarely do we see something earn this kind of unanimous praise, but our reviewer Luke Reilly would agree , giving GTA 6 a coveted score of 10 on our scale and calling it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played." However, you may have heard about the wide discrepancy between the critic's metascore and the user score — as of publishing this, GTA 6 has a 5.7/10 average from well over 100,000 user reviews. Why is that?
User scores on Metacritic are under far, far (and I mean far ) less scrutiny, allowing everyone and anyone to post their own review and score regardless of how much of the game they've actually played. This isn't anything new, and it’s been around on other sites that aggregate scores from the audience (like Rotten Tomatoes or an older version of GameSpot I used to use as a kid). As a result, you're likely to see more outliers or trolling, but mostly users who shoot from the hip to let their voice be heard. That leaves things susceptible to review bombing – typically, a wave of reactionary people who have motives beyond evaluating a game for what it is.
There are reviews that appear to have legitimate concerns, mentioning that GTA 6 might not be for them or align with their tastes. Among those concerns are a slow start that emphasizes slice-of-life style activities before action starts to pick up, dissatisfaction with the interactive layers for simple tasks, the frame rate being capped at 30 fps, or a general disinterest in what it's trying to do as an open-world action game. Maybe it didn't live up to their perceived "hype" with 13 years between series entries. However, you might be wondering why GTA 6 is the latest subject of what's clearly motivated review bombing with tons of "0" scores from a reactionary crowd.
I'm not going to pretend to give credence to clearly disingenuous reviews, but if you are genuinely curious, there are a significant number of reviews that decry GTA 6 for being "too woke" and a, uh, "cuck simulator” — the most unserious people, the incel crowd coming out of the woodwork, trying to fight a weird culture war over a game they likely either did not play or have barely played. GTA has always parodied the most ridiculous parts of American culture, and GTA 6 is no exception — now the primary targets of that satire are crying about it.
I don't think I need to explain what it means to be a "cuck" or the concept of cuckoldry, but by definition, it has nothing to do with anything that happens to you or that you have to do in GTA 6. And perhaps the most telling part of it all is the complaints of "woke" (another term that has been ground to a point of no meaning, co-opted by right-wing extremists to label anything they deem politically progressive).
In large part, GTA 6 is telling a love story where two partners, the protagonists Jason and Lucia, have a believable relationship on-screen with corresponding gameplay elements in addition to their Bonnie and Clyde-esque crime sprees. Maybe you don't want to put up drywall, renovate your house, or run errands in early missions, but what you're about to read is more telling about the kind of people review-bombing the game than the content of the game itself.
Sift through the negative reviews on Metacritic and it's a trove of entries that read, "Everything that represents the woke culture don’t deserve nothing, other than zero." Or, "GTA 6 is way too woke for my taste." And other variations on one that reads, "Graphics fantastic, besides that a cuckhold [sic] game, and really woke!" One just spams the word "woke" while several are straight gibberish or admittance that they did not play the game.
One entry reads, "I already have an annoying gf in real life and you want me to deal with it in the game again???????", while another says, "No hookers, no freedom, No action, Just cuck simulator, Please woke community, leave Rockstar games alone." And (sorry) one more for the road: "The plot is boring, and the main characters are a simp and a stereotypical ‘strong woman.’ They have absolutely no charisma; the game is packed with a one-sided agenda, and the trolling of ‘libturds’ is dull and predictable."
Amid this all, Metacritic has some measures in place to moderate fake reviews — it removed user reviews that went live before the game even released . And its 36-hour rule has been in place for a while where user reviews can't go up until a day-and-a-half has passed from a game's public release. Moderators also have the ability to stamp out reviews that violate Metacritic's guidelines, but with well over 100,000 of them up now, it's a gargantuan task.
While that crowd continues to be petty, whatever dent they think they're making isn't visible, as publisher Take-Two Interactive reported $3.79 billion in revenue with approximately 32.5 million units sold by launch day. Rockstar is going to be fine. Like the game or not, outrage fatigue is settling in; this perceived culture war is as meaningless as it's ever been, and it's best to pay it no mind to save yourself from the psychic damage.

pool.resumen:
Si os ponéis a ver las imágenes de satélite del Atlántico tropical entre marzo y octubre, seguramente os llame la atención la existencia de una inmensa mancha parduzca que atraviesa buena parte del océano . No se trata de un vertido ni de ningún otro desastre ambiental, sino de un organismo vivo en plena expansión que, comentan hoy los compañeros de GameStar en Alemania, se extiende a lo largo de 8.850 kilómetros desde África Occidental hasta el golfo de México.
Hasta tiene su propio nombre oficial. Se trata del Gran Cinturón de Sargazo del Atlántico , un inmenso entramado de algas flotantes que lleva años despertando el interés de investigadores como los de la Optical Oceanography Laboratory de la Universidad del Sur de Florida. Y no es para menos. pool.titulo: GTA VI rompe dos récords históricos de PlayStation
pool.resumen:
Se esperaba que el estreno de Grand Theft Auto VI fuera un evento de proporciones cósmicas, y los hechos han estado a la altura de las expectativas. Hace unos días descubrimos que el juego protagonizó el lanzamiento más exitoso de la historia del entretenimiento vendiendo más de 32,5 millones de copias antes del 19 de noviembre y ahora PlayStation ha anunciado que el mundo abierto de Rockstar también ha pulverizado todos los récords de la historia de la marca : desde el número de nuevas consolas hasta el recuento de usuarios simultáneos.
El lanzamiento más importante del año para PlayStation

En el mismo revelan que el juego fue jugado por un total de 39 millones de jugadores únicos durante el fin de semana de su estreno. Esto no necesariamente implica que se hayan vendido 39 millones de unidades solo en PlayStation, ya que si dos personas comparten consola pero juegan en diferentes cuentas se contabilizan como dos jugadores únicos distintos. En cualquier caso, las estimaciones ya hablan de 50 millones de unidades comercializadas.

pool.titulo: Witcher 4 Has Fewer People Working On It Than It Did 3 Months Ago, But Just Barely
pool.resumen:
As part of CD Projekt's latest earnings report, the Polish developer revealed new information about its projects and headcount.
For the quarter that ended on October 31, The Witcher 4 was the company's biggest project by headcount, with 513 people working on it. That's down from 519 people for the quarter that ended on July 31.
For comparison, the number of developers on Cyberpunk 2 rose from 184 to 199 and staffers on the new IP codenamed Hadar jumped from 33 to 34. The codename Sirius game, believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher game, saw its development staff shrink from 84 to 60; the project has undergone numerous shifts throughout its development as CD Projekt reworks the experience.
CD Projekt's total development headcount rose from 1,045 to 1,051.
In terms of money , CD Projekt reported Q3 revenue of 208 million PLN ($51 million USD) and net earnings of 109 million PLN ($26.8 million). CD Projekt spent a lot--more than 177 million PLN ($43.5 million) on development costs during the quarter--but the company's total cash reserves grew by 31 million PLN ($7.6 million USD).
CD Projekt has a number of big projects in the works, including The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past in 2027

It's not surprising, given the game's record-breaking start, with 32.5 million sales from preorders alone. On PS5, GTA 6 is the "biggest launch" in PlayStation history, and players spent an average of 17.4 hours playing in its first few days--which probably didn't leave much time for a quick browse of after-hours material.
According to Mashable , US traffic on Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched. Paradoxically, Pornhub traffic had actually been up by 16.5% compared to average days, likely indicating that people were bored and randy. pool.titulo: GTA 6 recomp leaders bail out as Take-Two cracks down on illicit efforts to get the game running on PC
pool.resumen: The leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recreate GTA 6 on PC, have quit the project, although others are still trying to carry it on.
pool.contenido:
Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.
The release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to quickly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, said on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon."
In a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead quickly.
But then things began moving quickly in a different direction. "I quit guys. I’m sorry," NotRexed, apparently the head of the project, posted last night on X . "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity."
Later, they added , "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye."
In a reply post, NotRexed stated explicitly that "Rockstar shut the server down," and shared an image of the copyright violation notice he'd received from Discord.
Shayder, who had previously predicted rapid progress on the Leonida effort following the release of the Xbox executable, took a more direct approach and simply deleted all of their X posts.
This isn't necessarily the end of work to bring GTA 6 (in a probably not-great state) to PC via AI. Other such projects are underway, and there also appears to be an effort to carry on with Leonida: The website remains up, with a new name attached as owner, and there's at least one Discord server dedicated to it, although it appears a little less focused at this point than the original Leonida server. A new Github repository (NotRexed also deleted that) has been set up: It's "a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project," according to a note on the project, which adds that "development continues here with its full commit history."
The advent of AI greatly simplifies and speeds up the work of bringing console games to PC (as long as you're not too picky about the quality), and that makes life tougher for companies that want to keep a lid on such projects. Still, it's not surprising that Take-Two and Rockstar are going hard on it: In the past, Take-Two has moved aggressively to shut down GTA 5 mod projects, an effort that culminated in its acquisition of the biggest and best of them . I've reached out to Take-Two for more information on the takedown and will update if I receive a reply.

pool.titulo: Attention strategy RPG sickos: The Fire-Emblem-style game that captured our hearts 4 years ago is back with a sequel
pool.resumen: Symphonic.
pool.contenido:
Four years ago (oh my god) strategy RPG Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga rather impressed our reviewer Jon Bolding. He wrote that "novel tactical mechanics make this indie a contender for the best strategy RPG this year".
Well, buckle up, 2027, because Symphony of War 2 has broken cover with a promise to release next year, and it's coming courtesy of the strategy sommeliers at publisher Hooded Horse, which I take as a very good sign.
SOW2 looks set to continue the Fire-Emblem-ish framework of its predecessor, tasking you with recruiting a gaggle of heroes to wage war with (and possibly compose symphonies, who's to say?) in "a world filled with political intrigue, betrayal, and tense, large-scale tactical battles". Which is a lot like our world, really.
It all looks very nice indeed. In the announcement trailer, we get glimpses of its squad-based combat and anime cutscenes, and I am officially into both. The art is poppy and distinctive, at some point an age-of-sail warship transforms into some kind of German WW1 destroyer, and the overworld triggers the regions in my brain devoted to thinking about Heroes of Might and Magic. Check, check, and check.
"Anime cutscenes!?" I hear you cry. "That sounds like the kind of thing that bespeaks a dense tapestry of lore I'll need to get to grips with first!" Well, apparently not. I am informed by Symphony of War 2's Steam page that the devs have no expectation you know what a "Nephilim Saga" even is before you pick this game up. "Symphony of War 2 is a standalone experience set several generations after the events of the first game—it can be enjoyed without having played Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga". The game's tale of a fallen empire trying to un-fall can be enjoyed single-serve .

pool.titulo: GTA 6 is great because of all its murderous NPCs, not in spite of them
pool.resumen: Nobody wants to work for their crimes anymore, smh.
pool.contenido:
It's come to my attention that some of us aren't having a very fun time with the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6 . I've seen videos and threads of players complaining about not being able to steal cars because of crack head drivers , getting hunted down by killer NPCs , and just generally having a harder time traversing Leonida because who knows what bloodthirsty beast hides behind each corner? And to this I say, your steak is too buttery? Your lobster too juicy?
My first interaction with one of the unfriendly residents of Leonida started when I accidentally bumped into their car. Because I am wholly unaware of my surroundings, I didn't even notice that anyone was mad at me as I listened to my pop songs and carried on driving towards my mission. Little did I know that right behind me was a four-wheeler with a driver who had steam coming out of her ears.
So I pull up to the side of the road, ready to head in and start my mission, when seemingly out of nowhere the four-wheeler comes barreling in, almost taking me out completely. The driver gets out and starts screaming about payback. I have no idea what I've done, but this is GTA 6, I'm not taking this slander. So I start swinging.
The fight ends with me knocking this lady out, but she doesn't go down without a fight. At one point, I actually thought that was it for me—taken out on the pavement by a soccer mum, what a way to go.
But even if I had taken a long sleep on the sidewalk, that would've been OK, because it's all part of the beautiful package that GTA 6 offers.
I don't want vapid NPCs that buckle at the first sight of a handgun, or have the object permanence of a goldfish. Filling Leonida with some actually competent, and dare I say dangerous NPCs makes this game infinitely more interesting. I like not knowing how one small action will ruin my whole day, or having to be a little wary of the people around me lest I want to incur a murderous chase across the city streets.
Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while.
I have a theory as to why players are pushing back against aggressive NPCs: they just don't like having to put in the effort after years of being able to do whatever they want in GTA Online. There's certainly some that will look back on the mostly timid NPCs of Los Santos and miss when all they had to do to steal a car was swing open its door and throw the limp driver out. Aside from shouting, there wasn't really anything a regular NPC could do to pose a threat to you back then.
Rockstar amped up the mayhem and carnage you could cause, turning it into a chaotic playground with few repercussions. GTA Online players have become accustomed to walking around like some vengeful god, wreaking havoc wherever or whenever they see fit, and only very occasionally dealing out mercy. Now these fickle deities have been forced to become human again.
A part of me understands the appeal. Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while. NPCs that actually have a backbone offer an experience that will keep me interested for far longer.
Plus, Leonida is based on Florida, do you honestly think you could terrorise the streets of Miami or Tampa Bay and walk out completely unscathed? Yeah, I thought as much.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 might play best when it hits PC, but it'll be best played with a controller
pool.resumen: I cannot get over all the ways Rockstar has turned a controller into an immersion tool.
pool.contenido:
I hate to credit Sony's aggressive (and presumably very expensive) marketing campaign for GTA 6—you know, the one which appeared to have also plucked the ability for Xbox to even mention the game by name. That's something I'm still shocked was even a thing anyone was allowed to do.
So I won't credit it… mostly. We all already know that PC is going to get the best version of GTA 6 when it finally hits our desktops, whenever that might be. But I am going to agree with one part of the whole "Grand Theft Auto 6 plays best on PS5" shtick: the DualSense controller. It's so good that I fear those who reach for a mouse and keyboard will be missing out on some incredible immersion.
In control I never expected a controller to actively add to my experience, but I also forgot just how many goodies Sony stuffed into this thing. Seriously, Rockstar has taken full advantage of everything the peripheral has to offer.
I've been weaving through traffic way more in GTA 6 thanks to a huge increase in general vehicle density and some criminally narrow roads that can cause some major bottlenecks. Flooring it all the way from A to B isn't quite as easy as it used to be, which is why I kind of love how you can use the adaptive triggers to comfortably maintain a steady cruising speed before clicking it all the way in as a way to floor it. It makes my speed feel just that little more deliberate, with that tactile feel for when I really want to amp up how fast I'm going.
But driving might actually be the least interesting way Rockstar has made full use of the controller. The parts that have gotten me more than anything are the small ways haptics have been implemented to strengthen story moments or make parts of Leonida feel even more alive.
The first time I really noticed the controller was back in the beginning of the game, when I'm instructed to go and pick Lucia up from prison. As I'm standing outside as Jason, watching her emerge from the gate, the controller starts thumping just a little bit. A heartbeat. I'm literally feeling Jason's heart racing as Lucia approaches. No dialogue, no internal monologue letting me know how nervous he is. It's such a small detail, but one that massively hammed up the moment for me.
My absolute favourite way it's been implemented, though? The clubs. The goddamn clubs. Leonida's sprawling nightlife is already impressive in isolation—Hitman's Berlin level was the last time I felt this enamoured with a videogame nightclub—but this is where Rockstar went all-in on the controller's haptic feedback. Step into a club and you'll immediately feel the bass pulsating through the controller.
It's not just the same, monorhythmic beat for every song though. The bass perfectly matches the song; those long, teeth-shaking booms cut with shorter, less intense thumps. I feel like I'm back in my first year of university trying to sleep while the nearby student nightclub blasts the same songs until 3am every damn Wednesday, the bass somehow reverberating across the campus and straight through my bedframe.
When I first set foot inside the Jack of Hearts club at the beginning of Chapter 3, I was practically stunlocked by how much more immersive being able to feel the bass through the controller was making the entire experience. Seriously, I cannot overstate just how much it sucks you into what's happening around you.
These are all things that I genuinely feel folks are going to miss out on with a simple mouse and keyboard. Sure, your aiming will be better. Yes, none of the things I've described above actually change anything about the gameplay. It'll still be the same GTA 6 no matter what you play with. But for all the ways Rockstar has managed to elevate the experience and the immersion I've been feeling just through something as small as the controller I'm holding? It at least deserves consideration for your go-to playthrough peripheral.

pool.titulo: Mass Effect writer says 'as a fan I would have been happy with the solution' they came up with for ME3's endings in ME Universe
pool.resumen: My personal solution would be playable elcor main character. Can't go wrong with that.
pool.contenido:
Spoilers for the end of Mass Effect 3 follow, naturally.
You know what? I didn't have many questions left at the end of Mass Effect 3. Joker was a robot now. His robot girlfriend was perhaps less of a robot? Shepard converted herself into a dotfile to make the Reapers chill out, and Buzz Aldrin's talents lie in areas other than voice acting.
I had plenty of questions when BioWare announced Mass Effect 5 was gonna be a thing though. Could you really write a Mass Effect story in the radically changed galaxy we were left with at the end of Shepard's adventure? Apparently, you could. In a recent AMA on Reddit (via IGN ), BioWare writer Cat Valente wrote that the now-cancelled Mass Effect sequel's team put a lot of work into handling ME3's endings "in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, [or] at least not piss them off completely".
The goal, says Valente, was to write a continuation of Mass Effect's narrative that "wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another". That tracks with what we've heard before: leaks have suggested ME5 was set to more or less wrap all the previous game's endings into one (Deus Ex: Invisible War style, hell yeah).
Of course, it'd have to do that while allowing BioWare "to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream videogame and not a post-modern 3000 page novel", adds Valente. "Not for nothing, guys, but that's *kind of a tall fucking order*. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be *really hard*".
The sheer challenge of creating a coherent, satisfying follow-up to ME3 that took into account everyone's choices had Valente, at one point, "thinking *god, if I'd known when I finished ME3 that I'd be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess...*".
Nevertheless, she reckons the studio did eventually alight on a way of handling it that made sense. "Yes, there was an answer, yes, I know it, as least inasmuch as I know what it was when I was working there… We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it".
And, well, that's that. We'll never know if the internet would have been satisfied or not (though I know where I'd put my money on that question), because EA killed the project and BioWare with it , and there's rarely a follow-up to an ending like that.

pool.titulo: World of Warcraft: Forever's been chasing bugs and gold exploits over the weekend—and now it turns out Sunder Armor might just not be working
pool.resumen: Lightning and sunder.
pool.contenido:
World of Warcraft: Forever 's absolutely had me enthralled, as per my review (and about 220+ hours of my actual life), but that's not to say there aren't issues. Over the weekend and going on into this week, Blizzard's had to play whack-a-mole with both exploits and what appears to be a long-standing bug affecting one of the tanking classes' core mechanics.
First, those exploits—players discovered that lockboxes contained a sort of quantum loot, in that the actual roll of the lockboxes seemed tied to the player peeking inside of them, rather than what was inside regardless. If you turned off auto-loot, you can open a lockbox without actually pulling the loot into your bag. Then, if you sent that lockbox to another player via mail, they'd get something different.
Essentially, players could simply play a game of mass pass-the-parcel to ensure favorable lockbox results, further busting up the economy after the Blackmaw Hold drama earlier this month. That's since been hotfixed , simply disabling the mechanic, with a more elegant solution to come further down the road: "Today, we’re working on a proper fix that restores the ability to peek and partially loot lockboxes, and makes them otherwise work as intended."
Meanwhile, the Obsidian Sentinel in Uldaman was briefly rendered lootless. As spotted by WoWHead , players could hop into the dungeon and repeatedly rinse the boss to grab a cheeky 18 or so gold in 15 minutes by vendoring the loot as a max-level character.
While that's not really game-breaking (instance lockouts are limited to five per hour), if you had an organised group of level 60s all funnelling gold to the same guy—like, say, if you were a streamer with a dedicated fanbase that didn't mind wasting a quarter of an hour, or if you were a large-scale RMT operation—there's a bigger problem.
That lootless state turned out to be a band-aid, as Blizzard simply lowered the vendor costs later.
Perhaps the biggest hiccup over the past weekend, though, is the fact that Sunder Armor (and other armor-reducing effects like faerie fire) very well might just not do anything. I hopped in-game to test it on my warrior and saw no noticeable difference between Sunder Armor in both dungeons and the overworld while fighting lower level targets, though my testing capabilities were limited solo, since armor is affected by the level of whoever's attacking the target: And if I rock up to an on-level elite in a dungeon at 60, I tend to die before I can get a good sample.
Fortunately, I don't need to be too thorough. There's a lot more comprehensive math and log-testing on this github post : "Once an armor debuff goes on, players' and pets' hits barely move, same as the report says. About 5% of the armor drop actually shows up in the damage, and more stacks don't help." The evidence is all pretty convincing.
While those other exploits are annoying oopsies, arguably just a result of players—who find edge cases like water finds cracks—stress-testing the system? The Sunder Armor bug is sort of huge, since that's one of the protection warrior's main group utilities (aside from being a tanky meatshield). It still appears to be filling its primary role of threat generation, but: Yikes.
There's no mention of it in the hotfixes , but I'll update this article if one pops up in the coming days.

pool.titulo: The Last of Us Part 2 Leaks Made Backlash Worse, Laura Bailey Says
pool.resumen: Abby actor Laura Bailey reflects on how pre-release leaks and online misinformation made The Last of Us Part 2's backlash so much worse.
pool.contenido:
The Last of Us Part 2 actress Laura Bailey has reflected on how the game's pre-release leaks and the subsequent spread of misinformation made its ensuing online backlash much worse.
More than six years after The Last of Us Part 2 leaks ignited controversy online and sparked a wave of death threats towards Bailey and her family, the prolific video game voice actress has now labelled Naughty Dog's highly-anticipated sequel as being "cursed" from the off.
While acknowledging that the game's bold narrative choices would always have been polarizing, Bailey blamed the level of vitriol directed specifically at her on the leaks of specific scenes involving her character Abby that spoiled major plot points — and did so without the game's intended narrative context. Because of this, she believes, online outrage had already hardened across social media long before launch day.
Warning! If you're still worried about The Last of Us Part 2 spoilers, now's a good time to head elsewhere.
"That game got cursed by so many different elements," Bailey said, appearing on the Mythical Kitchen podcast. "It got leaked, nobody knew the full story and all that got leaked were these horrific scenes. It had been leaked that there's a trans character in the game. The scene comes out where [Abby] has got a golf club. It just turned into a nightmare online.
"They were looking into all of the active death threats that were coming in," Bailey continued. "Because it was constant. They threatening my parents, they were threatening my baby."
The leak of various cutscenes in April 2020 — several months before The Last of Us Part 2's official release — led franchise steward Neil Druckmann to say he had been left "heartbroken" at their impact after working for years on the game. Naughty Dog issued an official statement pleading with fans not to spread the spoilers further online but, predictably, such was the fan investment in The Last of Us Part 1's duo of Ellie and Joel that word of the latter's abrupt murder by Abby spread quickly across the internet.
"I knew it was going to get a reaction because Joel is beloved and he is an amazing character," Bailey noted. "I loved him. I knew that was coming. But because of the leaks, it was just a lot. Up until then I was very present online and I shared a lot of my sense online. I kind of backed off after that.
"The haters are very loud online," she concluded, "but there's a ton of people that love that game and still come up at cons to me, and are dressed as Abbie and say she changed their life and it's an amazing game. And it is, it's beautiful and the message of it is beautiful."
Despite all of that, Bailey went on to win Best Performance at The Game Awards 2020, while IGN's The Last of Us: Part 2 returned a perfect 10/10 score.
Photo by Rodin Eckenroth/WireImage.

pool.titulo: Why Director Robert Eggers Calls His Brutal New Horror Movie Werwulf the Darkest Film He Has Ever Made
pool.resumen: Werwulf just might be drector Robert Eggers’ darkest film yet. So bleak and dark, in fact, that Eggers recalled “when Jarin Blaschke, my cinematographer, first read the script, he said, ‘Does this take place in Hell?’”
pool.contenido:
“It was after Nosferatu and I said, ‘What's the darkest thing I can write?’” filmmaker Robert Eggers recently told me about the genesis of his upcoming horror film, Werwulf . The film takes place in 13th century England and follows a farmer, simply called Man, who has been cursed to live as a werewolf.
“Werewolves [in medieval European folklore] were doing things that were so extreme and taboo and violent that the culture couldn't accept that they were human and so they called them werewolves,” Eggers said about the historical underpinnings of his film. “So I thought that this was going to be the right so-called creature to inhabit a very dark movie.”
Werwulf just might be Eggers’ darkest film yet. So bleak and dark, in fact, that Eggers recalled “when Jarin Blaschke, my cinematographer, first read the script, he said, ‘Does this take place in Hell?’” Eggers and Blaschke’s collaboration goes all the way back to the helmer's feature film directorial debut, 2015’s The Witch. They’ve since worked together on each of Eggers’ subsequent pictures ( The Lighthouse , The Northman , Nosferatu , and now, Werwulf).
“When I did more research about werewolf folklore, it's very different from what we've seen in cinema. I understood that this also gave me the opportunity to explore some things that I explored in The Witch and – for reasons of my own inexperience and talent at the time and also for reasons of budgetary limitations – couldn't quite do, and I got a chance to try it again [in Werwulf],” Eggers said.
“I think I've derided The Witch on many occasions but I am proud of the screenplay and the screenplay was good. And as Alfred Hitchcock said, the three things you need to make a great film are script, script, script, so I think that, for the people who really relate to The Witch, I think that that is why. And then The Lighthouse, I love The Lighthouse but there's barely a story. And The Northman's Hamlet and Nosferatu was Dracula and this is finally an original story with a driving narrative again.”
In this exclusive clip from Werwulf, which can be viewed via the player above , Aaron Taylor-Johnson’s Man has been drafted by the King’s wolf hunters to join them in pursuing the wolves that are killing the sheep pivotal to England’s wool trade , the country’s biggest economy. While on the hunt, the man has an eerie encounter with a wolf where, for lack of a better phrase, game recognizes game.
“Aaron is the only person who could have played this role. I wrote the role for him. He's a very handsome man in a traditionally masculine way; he can grow a huge beard [and] he also has a haunted quality to him, but he also has a dance background. So I knew that he would be capable of this incredible movement,” Eggers said. “And it was one of the things that excited me the most about what the werewolf transformations would be in this film, is that it is physically the actor doing most of it. Yes, David White, the special effects makeup designer, does more stuff after that, but I wanted it to be grounded in this body that is in agony.”
Taylor-Johnson worked for months with choreographer Marie-Gabrielle Rotie to perfect the movements required to portray the terror and pain of the werewolf transformations. The actor also took it upon himself to study wolves.
“I gave him a tremendous amount of research that I thought would be helpful, but it was something that I wasn't proposing that he wanted to do, [which] was to go to a wolf sanctuary and hang out with some real wolves,” Eggers recalled.
“It was one of the best things we did in prep also because it was something that I wasn't thinking of and it changed the film. It changed his physicality [and] the way that the alpha male wolf interacted with Marie-Gabrielle - she was there as well - influenced how Aaron's character interacts with Lily Rose [Depp], who plays his wife, physically. And then also the howl of the alpha male wolf being so close to him was really mind-blowing because, obviously, you have the high pitch mournful howl, but when you're a bit closer you also feel this subwoofer reverberating in my ribcage, not just the wolf's ribcage. It was really quite amazing. It was intimidating.”
Look for my full on-camera interview with Robert Eggers closer to when Werwulf opens in theaters December 25. Tickets to see Werwulf in 35mm are now available .

pool.titulo: 'I Made the Deal' – President Trump Takes Credit for Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia, Posts Bizarre AI Image to Celebrate
pool.resumen: Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia, with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.
pool.contenido:
Jensen Huang returned yesterday as CEO of Nvidia , with the company crediting "input from senior levels of the United States government." And, just in case that wasn't clear, Donald Trump has taken all the credit.
Yesterday, in an interview with CNBC , President Trump told reporters that he convinced Nvidia's board to take Huang back, saying he "made the deal" and that he "gave them assurances, at least everything we knew" that the CEO's return wasn't a risk to national security.
Trump also took to social media to celebrate after the announcement, even posting a meme with Jensen Huang in Donald Trump's place after the assassination attempt in Pennsylvania, but instead of raising a fist in defiance, Huang is holding up a red bra.
While Trump seems happy that Huang has returned, the reinstated CEO now has to face both houses of Congress in hearings about Nvidia's compliance with export controls. Politicians from both parties are demanding answers about how many GPUs have been exported to embargoed countries like China and Russia.
Massachusetts Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren posted on X / Twitter: "This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and Nvidia still owe Congress answers. The Trump Administration needs to explain what 'input' was given and by which senior officials to support Huang’s reinstatement."
What's more surprising is that Senator John Curtis, a Republican from Utah, echoed Warren's concerns, posting on X / Twitter: "Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?"
Despite these ongoing concerns, at least some Nvidia employees seem happy with Huang's return. An Nvidia employee posted a video on X / Twitter, below, of Huang getting a standing ovation in the lobby of the company's headquarters.
if you come for the king, you best not miss https://t.co/yb2eV1d5do
— abir (@aburducky) November 23, 2026
It's unsurprising that Huang would be welcomed back in this way, after an internal movement among employees to reinstate the CEO picked up quite a bit of steam immediately after his resignation. But while there was a crowd of cheering employees, there are at least some employees who feel like his return is a mistake, with one engineer anonymously telling Yahoo Finance : "This is the worst outcome. We already paid the price of his departure but are still saddled with working for a jerk."
In the fallout of Huang's departure, reports emerged that painted a picture of his management style. For example, he allegedly told one employee that he'd "pee on [their] brain."
It's still early days for Huang's return to Nvidia, and with everything that's happened in the last two weeks, it's impossible to guess what's going to happen next. But now that his return has breathed new life into the AI market, it's unlikely that RAM prices are going to come down any time soon.
