pool.titulo: Diablo 4 Season 16 Fixes One of the Biggest Problems With Helltide
pool.resumen: Diablo 4 Season 16: Season of Tyrael's Gambit officially kicks off on December 1. We finally know a bit more about what the new season holds in store, and it's going to make one of the biggest activities much less of a pain.
pool.contenido:
Diablo 4 Season 16: Season of Tyrael's Gambit officially kicks off on December 1. We finally know a bit more about what the new season holds in store, and it's going to make one of the biggest activities much less of a pain.
Season 15, Hell's Legacy, is a tough act to follow. It brought in a ton of nostalgic content like the Prime Evils, runewords, and even Whimsyshire. It does seem like a lot of that Anniversary content is going to be retired (I'll miss runewords), but at least it seems like Season of Tyrael's Gambit is going to make farming Helltides a bit less annoying.
In the patch notes for the new season , Blizzard says one Helltide will always be up in the vanilla zones, with another active in either Nahantu or Skovos, offset by 30 minutes. In practice, that means there will always be an active Helltide. That would be good enough on its own, but Blizzard is also changing the way Abberant Cinders work. Instead of expiring at the end of each Helltide, Blizzard is introducing a cap, and will let you carry cinders between Helltides.
For the uninitiated, that might not seem like a big deal, but it's a massive quality-of-life change. If you're not aware, Helltide is essentially an in-game invasion event, where demons overrun an area in the open world. You go in and kill demons for 55 minutes to get Abberant Cinders, which you can then use to unlock chests scattered throughout the zone. Helltides have always been one of the best ways to farm XP, and there have been several seasons that revolve entirely around them.
Now that War Plans, which were introduced with Lord of Hatred, are such a central part of how Diablo 4's gameplay loop works, there's always a chance that you're going to need to do bit of Helltide farming to progress. The problem was that Helltides spawned on a timer, and there was always a 5-minute gap between them. That doesn't sound too bad, but sometimes a Helltide would pop up in your to-do list and you'd either zone in with a mere 10 minutes to gather a ton of Cinders, or there simply wouldn't be a Helltide active. This new change solves both of those problems.
Now, even if you go into a Helltide with just a few minutes remaining, you can still gather Cinders without having to worry about opening 250 Cinders worth of chests before the timer expires. You can simply farm until the Helltide moves and then teleport to the next one. Easy. It's such a seemingly small change, but it's made me more excited for the 16th season of this ARPG than anything I've heard about it so far.
Beyond that, the Season of Tyrael's Gambit also brings changes to War Plans, where you'll be able to customize them to favor the activities you actually like doing. So, if you hate Helltide, even with the new changes, it sounds like you'll be able to make them appear a little less often in your War Plans.
The new season will also have a new item type called Horadric Items, which will synergize with set talismans. In the example Blizzard shared in its post, this could be as simple as adding +1 set count to your talismans to an ability that is only activated if you have a certain set of talismans equipped.
Seasons like this are a prime example of the way Blizzard will support Diablo 4 going forward, now that Diablo 5 is in the works. Diablo 4's director has come out and reassured fans that the game will continue to get new seasons as long as people are playing , and with how different Diablo 5 sounds so far , it's possible that Diablo 4 will have a long life ahead of it.

pool.titulo: The Witcher 4 Will Have a Comparable Leap From GTA 5 to GTA 6, Says CD Projekt Red
pool.resumen: CD Projekt Red expects a leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 that is comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6.
pool.contenido:
CD Projekt Red expects a leap between The Witcher 3 and 4 that is comparable to the one between GTA 5 and 6.
In a recent earnings call (via Eurogamer ), CDPR was peppered with questions about GTA 6, since the developer also makes ambitious open-world games. CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski was asked whether or not the studio is looking at GTA for inspiration and if people can expect a similar leap between games. He noted that they have, indeed, observed the jump between GTA 5 and 6 before stating that fans can expect something comparable for The Witcher 4.
"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 — I think so, yes," he said. "It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."
The leap between GTA 5 and 6 is pretty absurd. There's a significant number of more things to do, particularly for those interested in roleplaying as a criminal. You can steal drugs, rob banks, knock over virtually any store on the map, and so much more. A lot of these details were either reserved for scripted missions in GTA 5 or were underbaked as open-world activities, but are fully fleshed out for you to do however you want in GTA 6. Advancements in NPCs, interactivity, immersion, and the ability to enter hundreds of interiors also make GTA 6 feel a world apart from its predecessor.
Will The Witcher 4 also have tons of enterable interiors or deeper interactions with random NPCs? It's too soon to tell. It's possible that the leap for CD Projekt Red could come in a number of other ways, as The Witcher is a totally different world from GTA, after all. Maybe monster hunting will be more nuanced and involved than in The Witcher 3, similar to how GTA 6 has more engaging criminal activities.
CDPR also noted that it plans to find ways to expand the game to more mainstream audiences, like GTA 6 has. GTA 6 collaborated with major mainstream artists to create original music, in addition to bold marketing campaigns that made the game difficult to ignore.
The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release , and we can probably expect more looks at the game next year. CDPR also noted that it has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the game, which will also cover previous games and allow for opportunities with PlayStation Plus' services.

pool.titulo: 'Crazy Secretive' — GTA 6 Voice Actor Reveals Details of Rockstar's 'Humongous' NDA
pool.resumen: A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”
pool.contenido:
A voice actor who appeared in GTA 6 described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game, calling the project “crazy secretive.”
Issa Lopez is a voice actor who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, a Latin channel that plays reggaeton and dembow tracks featuring Spanish-speaking artists from the Caribbean and Latin America.
In a November 20 interview with Page Six , Lopez revealed that she recorded her lines for the station as recently as September 2026, and said the NDA she was made to sign before officially performing the part was comparable to the process of purchasing a home or a vehicle.
“Have you ever signed papers to buy a house? To buy a car? You know, it’s thick! It was a pretty humongous pack of papers that came with it. But I mean, it’s worth it! And I didn’t have to wait like all these other folks. Some of these folks have been working on this for like 10–11 years, you know what I mean?” she said.
She went on to describe the recording process for her lines, saying that she hadn’t seen anything until the day of the performance. With no time to prepare, she was essentially “put on the spot” — but she was so excited about the opportunity that she didn’t mind.
“In my usual voiceover gigs — let’s say you want me to do a commercial for you. I get a Zoom [link] maybe the day before, maybe the same day I get the script,” she explained. “Everything was like, popped up on the screen. It was mad cool. It was like, ‘You ready? And I’m like, ‘Uh-huh.’ You press a button and then boop, it pops on the screen, they say hello, and there’s a bunch of people in your ear. And they’re like, ‘Okay, here it is,’ and that’s when you see it. You are put on the spot. And you better bring it. And after that, I don’t know — whatever was in front of my face disappeared. “
Lopez revealed that she wasn’t told what the project was for, but figured it out based on context clues from an email titled “heard by millions,” saying she “read it and knew what it was for.” She also didn’t know that Bad Bunny would be co-hosting the Cocoteo station alongside her, leading to a wild realization once Rockstar released the radio stations before the game actually came out.
“We knew nothing. I saw the liners, and when I saw the liners I was like, ‘Okay, I know why I got the gig.’ ‘Cause it was like Puerto Rican dot com. It was super easy. But it was so cool, because Rockstar let me be myself. …they were like, ‘Issa, we want natural. Whatever you got, we want,'" she said.
The actors in GTA 6 were extremely secretive about their involvement in the project. Most notably, actress Manni L. Perez, who plays Lucia, was under immense pressure after fans sleuthed her social media accounts and figured out it was her before she could officially reveal the information. Now, she’s up for best performance at The Game Awards, which is one of eight nominations the game has secured mere weeks before the show takes place this December.
Other performers who have finally revealed their involvement in the game are Mandy’s actress, Lexie Shoaibi , as well as the voice and performance artist for Jason Duval, Dylan Rourke . Rockstar released the full credits for the game, too, which you can check out here — just beware of spoilers if you haven’t finished it yet.

pool.titulo: The difference between The Witcher 3 and Witcher 4 will be 'comparable' to that of GTA 5 and GTA 6, CD Projekt boss says: 'I mean, it's been 11 years'
pool.resumen: CD Projekt Red reported its Q3 earnings today, but all anyone wanted to talk about was GTA 6.
pool.contenido:
CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.
Perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6. While CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski didn't go too deep on the topic, he did say that the upcoming Witcher 4 will be comparable to GTA 6 in at least one way.
"Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski said when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6. "Having said that, of course, I'm not going to make a deep dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course, we did look at the game. We did see the differences.
"Do we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."
Well, sure. As Nowakowski said, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was released 11 years ago, and it'll be two more years before The Witcher 4 comes out—assuming it's not delayed, which would make it a rarity among CD Projekt games. It will also be the same number of years between Witcher 3 and 4 as spanned GTA 5 and 6. In the world of technology, 13 years is a long time.
Hell, just the upgrade from the original Witcher 3 to the remastered version that dropped earlier this year is notable:
Original Remastered At the same time, Nowakowski said that while the GTA 6 launch was tremendously successful, CD Projekt Red doesn't intend to merely mimic Rockstar's approach when The Witcher 4 is ready to go: "Our games are different and the require a certain different approach, and we just do certain things differently than they do."
He also said that while the release of GTA 6 has had an impact on Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 sales on consoles, he doesn't expect it to have a "material impact" on the company's Q4 finances for one obvious reason.
"You do have to remember that a lot of our players are also PC-based," Nowakowski said. "GTA has not launched on PC. We have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales on engagement." And, he added, "on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero."
Nowakowsi also said that GTA 6 hasn't changed CD Projekt's ambitions for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2: If anything, it's "an inspiration in many ways for our developers." And he's not concerned about its success pushing up development budgets, because CD Projekt's games "are not budget-driven developments."
"I'm not saying that we don't care about the budgets. We do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well," Nowakowski said. "But you cannot make games like that having in mind, 'This is the fixed number of money I want to spend, and that's it. Otherwise, we're gone.'
"They are ambition-driven developments and money is important. The budgets are not indefinite. That's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is kind of like I said. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release. It has just always been like that."
Nowakowski's positive take on GTA 6 isn't too far off that of Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski, who said yesterday that he's suffering from " GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression ," although he quickly clarified that CD Projekt is "doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor." (And that he wasn't being serious about cancelling Cyberpunk 2.)
seriously though i think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor. GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed

pool.titulo: Analyst estimates Call of Duty lost 44% of its players when GTA 6 came out, and unlike fans of its live-service competitors they've been slow to come back
pool.resumen: Turns out Fortnite players are more loyal.
pool.contenido:
Sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a new record for concurrent PlayStation players , which isn't bad for a game that's currently only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.
Alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active users drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the company's estimates.
Fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims, with an estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend, and EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 launched," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M."
But where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott says: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline."
During that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece is the way to do it.
As Elliott concludes, this is only part one of the story. When Rockstar comes back for the second bite of this apple its rivals might have an even harder fight on their hands: "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 hits (some time next year simultaneously, I'd imagine), then the bounce back will not be so obtainable."

Meanwhile, Durin and his family are banished from Khazad-dûm but make off with one of the rings given to the Dwarf-lords. That’s the last we’ll see of their storyline until next season as the Dwarves sat out the season finale.
“The Doom of Men” finally resolves the Gandalf/Dark Wizard storyline with Pallando sacrificing himself to save Gandalf’s in a classic Heel-Face Turn ending in redemptive death . Gandalf freed his old friend from the corrupting influence of the ring, which Pallando had apparently worn for all of an evening before Gandalf tricked him. (Pallando’s wearing of the ring last long enough for there to be an allusion to Gollum’s iconic “my precious” line.)
More From Middle-earth:
The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 1-4 Review
The Rings of Power Season 3, Episodes 5-6 Review
While the wizards vs. Nazgnagôl battle felt awkwardly executed with all its obvious wire-work, at least it provided Gandalf and Pallando a few moments to finally fight side-by-side as allies. I’m not sure, though, if the Pallando storyline was ultimately worth taking up so much dramatic real estate over the last two seasons for such a brisk payoff. At the very least, Pallando’s death and the resulting liberation of his followers robbed Sauron of a good chunk of his army.
I enjoyed how Sauron tested Gandalf’s incorruptibility in a very Last Temptation of Christ manner, offering him the rule of Middle-earth if he’d just submit. I also liked Sauron’s short-lived ruse of conjuring a figment of Nori Brandyfoot (Markella Kavenagh in a cameo) in an attempt to dupe Gandalf, although I never believed that the show was bringing back Nori in any real way.
Elrond evoking his brother to help instill some hope in the Númenórean soldiers on the eve of their likely deaths was a nice touch. Despite a moment where he allows himself to ask the advice of Galadriel and Celeborn – whose relationship woes I haven’t found particularly interesting thus far – Pharazôn’s hubris ultimately gets the better of him. The Elves foresee the Doom of Men when Sauron surrenders so I fully expect Season 4 to end with The Fall of Númenor.

pool.contenido:
Famous Dutch-Belgian race driver Max Verstappen revealed that he’d spent the weekend of the Las Vegas Grand Prix locked in to GTA 6, saying he played over 40 hours of the game.
Everyone’s got GTA 6 fever, including Max Verstappen. Not even the Las Vegas Grand Prix could stop him from causing virtual chaos in Vice City, which he says he spent more than 40 hours doing during the weekend of the race.
Verstappen nonchalantly dropped this nugget of information during a live stream the following week, saying he would play the game in the mornings and evenings in between his duties on the track.
“I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas,” Verstappen explained. “I mean, I can’t go out anyways and walk around.”
The driver also revealed that he’s been so focused on GTA 6 and driving real-life race cars that he’s “completely forgotten” how to play Minecraft, despite having a scheduled stream for it.
“I’m so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can’t, I just can’t!” he joked.
🤯Max Verstappen played GTA VI for FORTY HOURS while in Las Vegas
On top of that, he also won the race https://t.co/jwuxQnHxyS
— Pablo Martinez (Holiness) (@F1BigData) November 24, 2026
The Las Vegas Grand Prix took place on November 19 - 21. Verstappen took first place in the prestigious Formula 1 race, beating out Britain’s Lando Norris and Australia’s Oscar Piastri. The race is around 50 laps long with a total race distance of 192.6 miles (309.96 kilometers), generally lasting around one and a half hours.
As revealed by the name, Grand Theft Auto is a game series that involves a lot of vehicles, and not just for carjacking; the latest entry in the franchise even features drag racing and mudding, a hobby common in the American countryside that involves the use of off-road vehicles racing through mud-covered areas or even specially-made racetracks.
It’s quite likely that Verstappen dabbled a bit in these side missions, though he says that he’s already beaten 80% of GTA 6’s story. In fact, the driver admitted that he has skipped most of the main cutscenes, calling them “too boring.”
Verstappen’s style of playing GTA 6 is one of several that we’ve seen over the weekend. In fact, many players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of spending time in Chapter 1, which sees Jason living the average life of a drug runner in Rockstar’s fictionalized version of the Florida Keys. Oddly, it’s a slow-paced, slice-of-life section of the game that some players haven’t left yet, preferring to take it easy diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and soaking up the environment.

pool.titulo: Some GTA 6 Fans Love Chapter 1 for Its Slower Pace and Are Spending Dozens of Hours Roleplaying in It
pool.resumen: GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.
pool.contenido:
Warning: This article features light spoilers for the early hours of GTA 6 .
GTA 6's first chapter has been somewhat divisive due to its slower pace, but it's also a part of the game that some fans have spent dozens of hours playing due to it highly immersive slice-of-life elements.
Instead of throwing you headfirst into crazy heists or explosive set pieces, the first chapter of GTA 6 is largely spent bumbling around Rockstar's version of the Florida Keys. You can go fishing, scuba diving, and even fix up your house before Lucia's release from prison. It's an exceptionally low-key and chill opening to a game filled with all kinds of crazy action, which is why it's also rubbed some people the wrong way. They don't want to do chores or kick it on the beach; they want to cause some mayhem.
However, for others, this has become an unexpected hook for GTA 6 that actually delayed their interest in getting to the meat of Rockstar's open-world epic. Various fans of the game have said they spent anywhere from 10 to as many as 40+ hours in just Chapter 1 alone. Keep in mind, this is a sliver of the overall experience, and much of the game's most interesting activities don't get added until subsequent chapters. However, some players just enjoyed living inside of this part of the game before things go horribly wrong and they're forced to start ramping up the violence and crime.
"Best thing about that early chapter is just how low stakes and casual it feels," said X user @CS11__ after spending 41 hours in Chapter 1 alone. "I forced myself not to go farther than Hamlet, so I really only ever experienced these two small areas in 40 hours. [...] The game hardly opened up, but it still felt unbelievably rich and fun."
But... what is it these people are actually doing, if not blowing stuff up and creating tons of chaos? Some fans were just going through the motions, giving themselves daily routines that involved working out, taking on relaxing hobbies, and exploring.
"[A] lot of roleplaying, day-to-day living type stuff," said Aaron Espionza on X , who estimated that he spent around 15–18 hours before picking up Lucia from prison. "I had a routine even when I would wake up, drive to the juice bar down the street, get my orange juice, and then say hello to the locals. If anyone said anything mean, I would get violent and throw empty juice cups at them. [I] did the workout routines. Basketball was a favorite of mine. Side stuff with Cal fishing, Donnie pick-ups, and scuba. But so much of it was testing how much detail Rockstar put into it. 'If I do this , will they do that ?' type of systems exploration. Always came away surprised."
X user @scaasm noted that the lower stakes nature of Chapter 1 even prompted him to follow traffic laws and use manual turn signals in GTA 6: "I follow traffic laws unless I'm doing something criminal, and generally just taking it very slow. [I'm] loving every moment."
The location itself was also a big driving point for a lot of fans, some of whom have personal connections or apprecation for its real life counterpart: "As someone from Florida, I think the Keys is one of those locations that they absolutely nailed (waning sands outlets too; they look exactly like the Orlando ones)," said @piterparker69 on X . "It felt kinda uncanny driving around (especially the 7 Mile Bridge) because of how good it replicates real life."
"I have been obsessed with the Florida Keys for the last 5 years, and finding out you spend the start of the game there, catching fish, fixing my house, working out, and just vibing gave me little motivation to move on," said @AnchormanV2 on X after spending roughly a dozen hours in Chapter 1.
"I took my sweet time in Key Lento, not necessarily to avoid progressing the story, but more so [bcause] I was just having so much fun exploring the keys and just taking it all in," said X user @HorrorUntitled . "There’s just so much to see to see and happening. It’s very overwhelming."
Of course, some people did get into a bit of open-world crime as well, or explore a bit beyond the Keys, but a lot of it was still a result of the story feeling low-stakes and not having much urgency in its first chaper. X user Ryan Ranc even noted that he would go around Key Lento acting as a vigilante: "I’m playing as Batman and roaming at night on my motorbike stopping crime."
Chapter 1 in GTA 6 is a very interesting piece of the game, and some even noted that they longed for that tranquility after moving on in the story. It's an intentional slow burn, as things get turned up to an 11 at the end of the chapter and make you come to appreciate what you had. It's the calm before the storm in many ways, and some people are really basking in that.

Tal y como apuntaba el psiquiatra Javier Quintero , la psicología llevaba años buscando comprender cómo funcionaba el sentimiento de amistad y, en 2022, investigadores de la Universidad de Nicosia dieron con la clave.
Tras analizar 50 rasgos deseables y otros 43 que solemos evitar , pidieron a 706 participantes que valorasen los primeros y a otros 865 que hiciesen lo propio con los segundos. Podríamos pensar que tener cosas en común, como que nos gusten los videojuegos, deberían estar en los puestos más altos, pero nada más lejos de la realidad.
Qué buscamos realmente en nuestros amigos

pool.titulo: Yes, There Was One Thing Cut from GTA 6 for Australia, NZ
pool.resumen: Rockstar chopped out a temporary stat buff from GTA 6, although players down under may not ever really notice it.
pool.contenido:
The Australian version of Grand Theft Auto 6 does differ from the international version in one small way; players down under are not able to use cocaine from their personal inventory to briefly overpower their stamina bar. NZ reportedly has the same version.
In GTA 6, baggies of cocaine can be collected (or skimmed from full bricks) and show up as a consumable on the item wheel in the same section as cigarettes, cigars, and joints. Using one triggers a buff that puts stamina in an overpowered state, albeit only for about 30 seconds. This function was never included in the Australian-specific version of the game, as it would have prevented GTA 6 from being classified in the country until it was removed. Australia’s classification laws allow illicit drug use in games, but using them can’t provide the player with gameplay benefits.
Overpowering your stamina (and everything else) is still possible via the use of adrenaline in the Australian version of GTA 6, and it’s also still possible to drink and smoke whenever you want. The general use of cocaine in story moments also still remains in the Australian version of GTA 6, because these instances aren’t associated with any in-game buffs.
While the caveat that forbids rewards for illicit drug use is bespoke to Australia – and doesn’t apply to NZ – NZ’s rating system (which does piggyback on some Australian and UK classification decisions for unrestricted content ) has its own idiosyncrasies. These recently caught out IllFonic’s recent Halloween multiplayer game , which was refused classification in Australia for illicit drug use linked to an incentive or reward (that is, that use of the drug provides a gameplay advantage to the player). Halloween since made its way to NZ, but not Australia. Since this is not Rockstar’s first rodeo, it knew exactly the tweak GTA 6 would require to skirt this continuing quirk in Australian video game ratings and avoid multiple submissions.
GTA 6 arrived late last week, crushing records and becoming the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with retail sales soaring to $3.79 billion in its first 24 hours. In my review for IGN I called it “the single most impressive video game I have ever played,” a sentiment shared by developers similarly stunned by how radically advanced it is.
Just getting started in GTA 6, or wondering what to do next? You can get stuck into the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN, consult our Beginner's Guide or Leonida interactive map , or get an idea of all the incredible flourishes to keep an eye out for by checking out our look at 99 incredible details you can find in GTA 6.

I've become utterly invested in keeping Jason and Lucia in love, which means a lot of my time in the game has been spent doing things with my partner in tow. Hitting the gym, inviting them out for a late-night bite, robbing a few jewellery stores. You know, couple things. Things couples do.
And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk. A lot. And you know what? Some of the best nuggets of information about their lives—both their time spent together before the events of the game, and their own individual lives before meeting one another—are tucked away in these interactions that fill the game's quieter moments.
Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny. Lucia poking fun at Jason for his deep voice and monosyllabic responses, or them reminiscing about little moments that happened in their relationship before the whole "Lucia ghosting Jason and ending up in jail" thing. Sometimes it's Lucia getting a spam call and giving the bot (and eventual human) on the other end of the phone an absolute earful.
But then, occasionally, beyond all the comedic conversations and flavour dialogue that give these characters so much life, the game'll drop some proper good lore. I'll do my best not to spoil stuff here, but for almost every complaint I've seen on social media about why certain protagonists did certain things, there's an answer tucked away in these interactions. The kind of things you'd really want to know about these characters? Your best chance of finding it all out is when you bring them together.
I've really enjoyed having lore drops unfold in mundane conversations while walking around, driving, or eating a burger, rather than hamfisted into the main story. They feel like natural breathing moments for the couple to recount the past, or get into the stuff that was happening in the time that they were apart. You know, the exact kind of times actual couples and friends would find the time to dig into these things in real life, too.
That doesn't mean you have to keep them together all the time. Some of their exclusive missions also provide a great bit of insight into their backstories—like Jason's side stuff with ex-army pal Bret Vogel, or the missions that have Lucia in some all-too-real situations with her mother.
I've played plenty of the game flying solo as both protagonists too, and you'll occasionally get some of this nattering just by hanging around in your abode together. But I can't recommend enough that you find plenty of opportunities to bring them together out in the open world. Even if it's just for 15 minutes here and there, you'll uncover a whole lot about who they were before we first got to know them as the player. And as someone who has really enjoyed learning just about everything about these two as I can, it's been one of my favourite parts of the game so far.

pool.titulo: GTA 6 Analysis Shows PS5 Version Suffers 'Substantially' More Frequent Frame Rate Drops Than Xbox Series X Version, Sparking Debate About Sony's 'Plays Best on PS5' Marketing
pool.resumen: The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6, and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5.
pool.contenido:
The tech experts at Digital Foundry have revealed their analysis of GTA 6 , and found the game performs “meaningfully better” on Xbox Series X than the base PS5.
Sony’s high-profile marketing deal for GTA 6 involved the key phrase, “Plays Best on PS5,” and while that marketing tagline encompasses more than just performance, many are now questioning its validity with GTA 6 out in the wild.
Digital Foundry found that Xbox Series X provides a “virtually identical visual presentation” to the PS5 in terms of overall image clarity and presentation quality, but there is a significant split on performance.
As Rockstar had announced before launch, GTA 6 “targets” 30 frames per second across all platforms, from the Xbox Series S up to the PS5 Pro, but there are moments where the frame rate drops. According to DF’s analysis , the frame rate suffers more on PS5 than Series X.
Here's what DF said on the issue:
PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips. Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off. Of course, the PS5 Pro version offers the best experience in terms of performance, but it’s interesting to see the Xbox Series X outperform the PS5 here. Some are pointing to non-performance related features, such as the PS5’s haptic feedback, which is great for driving, as playing a role in the phrase “Plays Best on PS5,” and we should be used to marketing speak that is technically not wrong by now. But, as DF reveals, when it comes to performance, there can be no doubting the clear winner.
Indeed, some are calling the “Plays Best on PS5,” phrase “grossly misleading,” claiming that Sony should have said “Plays Best on PS5 Pro” instead.
“I’ve been f***ing fooled,” one person said in the comments of DF’s YouTube video . “They did kind of say in the fine print that ‘best’ referred to the features in the DualSense controller,” another person countered.
“If you are advertising ‘Plays best on X’ to gamers, the immediate thought is going to be ‘Out the two places I can play the game, it is going to play the best on the X console,’” another suggested. “What does ‘Play’ mean to that audience? Performance, stability, possibly higher resolution, less texture pop-in.”
In June, when Sony trumpeted the “Plays Best on PS5” marketing line , it highlighted how GTA 6 takes advantage of the PS5 DualSense controller's haptic feedback and integrated speaker. Sony also highlighted its Tempest 3D AudioTech, which allows you to "surround yourself in the distinct soundscapes of Leonida" through its "highly accurate audio positioning." GTA 6 would also "leverage the PS5's ultra-high speed SSD" to experience GTA 6 "with near-instant load times." Sony's blog post made no mention of performance.
Meanwhile, there are questions around GTA 6’s use of FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series S version of the game only . Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, which makes GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox. It’s thought this tech is what made GTA 6 possible at 30fps on the underpowered Series S in the first place.
Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game instead use Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro uses Sony’s PSSR upscaler. But why not use FSR 4.1 on the Xbox Series X version of GTA 6 also? Similarly, if the PS5 version already supports PSSR, why not use Sony’s AI upscaling model QSSR (Quick Spectral Super Resolution)?
Elsewhere, fans are just marveling at the performance of GTA 6 on Xbox Series S, which — as we’ve reported — shows what Microsoft’s cheaper console is capable of. Ultimately, DF is hoping Rockstar releases GTA 6 updates that improve performance across the board, potentially adding 120Hz VRR support on PlayStation hardware and “stabilising” base console frame rates.

pool.titulo: Las abejas sin aguijón de Perú son los primeros insectos del mundo en obtener derechos legales y la ciencia ficción te explica por qué
pool.resumen:
Las abejas sin aguijón de la Amazonía peruana ya tienen derecho a existir, a prosperar, a vivir en un hábitat libre de contaminación y a que alguien las represente ante un tribunal cuando les hagan daño. Lo cuenta esta semana CNN en un reportaje de su serie Llamado a la Tierra. En octubre de 2025, la provincia de Satipo aprobó la primera ordenanza del mundo que reconoce derechos a un insecto , y en diciembre se sumó Nauta, en Loreto. Detrás está la bióloga Rosa Vásquez Espinoza , fundadora de Amazon Research Internacional , que lleva años recorriendo la selva con los pueblos indígenas para documentar a estas abejas, con el apoyo legal de Earth Law Center.
Perú tiene al menos 175 especies de abejas sin aguijón , y hasta hace muy poco su legislación solo protegía a la abeja europea, introducida en América, cuando a las meliponas las cultivan los pueblos indígenas desde hace siglos. Hoy se enfrentan a la deforestación, a los pesticidas, al cambio climático y a la competencia de especies invasoras como las abejas africanizadas, las famosas abejas asesinas. ¿Por qué son importantes? pool.resumen: Star Trek: Nemesis is streaming free on Pluto TV. Here's why the Next Generation cast deserved a better big-screen farewell.
pool.contenido: Saying goodbye to beloved television characters is never easy. After spending years getting to know them, audiences have expectations about how their stories should end. Unfortunately, 2002's Star Trek: Nemesis falls into the latter category, bringing an unceremonious end to the big-screen adventures of the Next Generation crew.

pool.titulo: Witcher 4 Won’t Be A PS5 Exclusive After New Deal With PlayStation
pool.resumen:
CD Projekt Red and Sony Interactive Entertainment just announced a marketing deal for The Witcher 4 , but that doesn't mean the game will be exclusive to PlayStation.
CD Projekt Red's Michał Nowakowski said on social media , "Just to be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain multiplatform."
The marketing deal could be similar to the one between Rockstar and Sony for GTA 6, where GTA 6 was given preferential treatment on PS5 in a number of ways in the marketing campaign.
Beyond The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red is making Cyberpunk 2 , a new IP codenamed Hadar , a new game believed to be a multiplayer The Witcher title , and a remake of the original Witcher . On the mobile side, CD Projekt Red is working with Scopely on a new game that hasn't been announced yet.
The Witcher 4 now has more than 500 people working on it , and the game is expected to release in 2028. Given that timing, The Witcher 4 likely won't be on a disc because Sony won't support game discs beginning in January 2028.
That being said, CD Projekt Red is promising that The Witcher 4 will have some kind of physical goodies for fans.

pool.titulo: The Witcher 4 Wants To Be The GTA 6 Of The Witcher Franchise
pool.resumen:
There's been a massive gap between new entries in The Witcher series, and for The Witcher 4 , developer CD Projekt Red aims to make it the GTA 6 of the series, with a noticeable leap in quality. In its Q3 earnings call, the studio says it has been inspired by the technological and gameplay advancements Rockstar Games has made with GTA 6--especially when compared to 2013's GTA 5--and hopes players will feel the same way when they jump into The Witcher 4.
"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski (via Eurogamer ). "But I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4--I think so, yes. It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

pool.titulo: How to steal an ATM and get a winched vehicle in GTA 6
pool.resumen: Yank out ATMs and grab the cash with Yasmani's tips.
pool.contenido:
Stealing an ATM in GTA 6 requires a few different things: a winched vehicle to haul it out of the wall and drive off, plus the dye pack jammer that stops marked bills from exploding pink all over your lovely cash.
There are two ways to get a winched truck. The video above shows a location at the crop duster landing strip in Frogswater where you can steal one, but you can also mod any truck at a mod shop to add a winch.
If you don't have a truck to mod, there's a unique one you can steal from the Kolt & Associates June Warehouse robbery in Port Gellhorn, just south of Sarena's Bargain Store, which you could then register with Moses and mod at Wasteland Off-Road in the north of the town.
You'll also need the dye pack jammer, which you get in the Chapter 3 main mission, Credit Check, for Raul. Once you have both of these, you're ready to rob an ATM. If you complete all three of Yasmani's jewelry thefts (also in Chapter 3), he'll call a little later and offer tips about full ATMs, giving you three for free that you have a 24 hour window to hit. Here's how to steal them
Reverse the winched vehicle into the ATM and lower the hook with the stick until it attaches. Drive at full speed to pull the ATM out and get some distance from the sounding alarm—this will summon the cops. Smash the ATM into stuff by swerving the truck to make it spill the cash boxes Get out, kick them, and quickly grab the marked bills in each. For Yasmani's tipped-off ATMs I got about 11k-ish per time, so not terrible, but likely not the best way to make money unless you get really efficient at it and invest in a proper getaway winch truck.

pool.titulo: Even Max Verstappen has succumbed to GTA 6 fever, squeezing in 40 hours around his Las Vegas Grand Prix win
pool.resumen: What's your excuse?
pool.contenido:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has managed to get its claws into just about everyone. Honestly, I can't go anywhere without hearing something from the soundtrack or someone talking about how much fun it is to joyride around Leonida. And now it's even infested the sports I watch.
To keep non-Formula One fans up to speed, it was the Las Vegas Grand Prix over the weekend, one of the newer circuits on the calendar. Third place went to Oscar Piastri. In second place was his McLaren teammate and previous world champion for 2025, Lando Norris. And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. But it is a little more impressive when you take into account that Verstappen has also put 40 hours into GTA 6, much of which would have been before the race.
"I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he says in a stream (via IGN ), correcting the idea that he actually spent the plane ride home playing GTA 6 instead of spending time doing so around the race. "I mean I can't go out anyways [in the evening and morning], and walk around."
Verstappen did, however, explain that the aspect that GTA 6 has likely affected the most is his ability to play Minecraft, which he had planned to stream later this week: "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't."
GTA 6 to Minecraft is certainly a jump, but you can't really blame anyone for trying to maximise their time in Leonida right now. I'll also take any chance to spend every free moment playing the game, the only difference being that instead of subsequently competing in an F1 race and winning it, I spend the next day of work acting like a zombie—a poorly functioning one at that. I suppose people are just built differently, or at least that's what I'll tell myself while I'm on my third cup of coffee in three hours.

pool.titulo: Tangles Review
pool.resumen: Tangles Review: The Gay Nineties collide with a high-strung Jewish family in a shattering animated film about dementia.
pool.contenido:
Tangles is in theaters in New York and Los Angeles on Nov. 27. It will expand to a wider release in January.
The weight of memory is vital to the biographical animated feature Tangles, a black-and-white story about family, the queer ‘90s, and above all else, early-onset Alzheimer’s. Based on the sparse but powerful 2012 comic by Sarah Leavitt — who co-wrote the screenplay with Trev Renney and director Leah Nelson — the film employs abstractions in its margins and connective tissue, making room for straightforward drama that proves incredibly moving in its unearthing of lived experience.
Beginning with a childhood flashback, Tangles introduces us to middle-aged Midge (Julia Louis-Dreyfus), based on Leavitt’s mother, as she helps a young Sarah (Fern Grandin) fight invisible monsters in her bedroom, with the help of a flashlight which Sarah imagines as a fuchsia lightsaber. Midge is, for all intents and purposes, Sarah’s superhero, but life goes on as the film skips forward to 1999. The adult Sarah, voiced by Abbi Jacobson, draws for a queer magazine in San Francisco, but a return to her hometown for a family visit proves a major turning point. Everyone including Sarah’s soft-spoken father Rob (Bryan Cranston), her idiosyncratic aunts Debbie (Pamela Adlon) and Sukey (Sarah Silverman) and her lively sister Hannah (Beanie Feldstein) seems to dance around major changes in Midge’s lifestyle and cognitive function.
They blame it, at first, on menopause, and then on Midge losing her job and her ensuing depression, but minor tasks prove frustrating and confusing for the usually gentle 50-something, who’s drawn with appropriately haggard squiggles. It takes a while before a real diagnosis tells them what might be wrong: an early form of dementia. This forces Sarah to fly back and forth between her family and her supportive, stud girlfriend Donimo (Samira Wiley), a schism of time, place and culture that slowly wears on her as Midge’s disease advances.
The dynamic between Sarah’s queer, urban environment and her nominally accepting but high-strung Jewish family allows the film to traverse different modes of expression and conversational rhythm, as she tries to be in two places at once. This dichotomy also helps enhance periods of nerve-wracking transition during lengthy travel, expressed through tongue-in-cheek formal flourishes. Each flight, for instance, becomes the venue for dreamlike jokes about Sarah’s deep-seated anxieties delivered over the plane’s PA system, leaving her vulnerable and exposed.
Louis-Dreyfus delivers a heartrending, piercingly realistic vocal performance as a woman trying to hold on to what little of herself she can find. Sarah is a character perpetually on edge, a baseline made all the more volatile when she takes it upon herself to recognize her mother’s illness and care for her as best she can, even at the cost of her various relationships. Midge, meanwhile, slips away gradually over the film’s 102 minutes, as Louis-Dreyfus delivers a heartrending, piercingly realistic vocal performance as a woman trying to hold on to what little of herself she can find.
The period setting is rendered with appropriate details — a few too many Marvel references aside, it feels like a sketched memory of the late 1990s, from pop culture to the textures and technologies — but the story itself is timeless. Nelson brings Leavitt’s autobiographical tale to life with generosity, imbuing each supporting character with a palpable denial that feels, at first, like a mere quirk, before revealing itself to be a coping mechanism. The gradual confusion and anger involved (both for Midge and her caretakers) results in a moving portrait of helplessness in the face of a brutal disease, as well as the few moments of love people are able to steal from it while they still can. By the time the film wraps up, its echoes of Midge in earlier scenes continue to loom large thanks to Louis-Dreyfus’ fine-tuned performance as she leaves quiet gaps in her wake, alongside a sense of longing for the character she used to be.

pool.titulo: Take-Two Appears to Be Trying to Scrub GTA 6 PC Ports From the Internet, as Vibecoders Race Toward Controversial World First
pool.resumen: Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game.
pool.contenido:
Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game.
This week, Cyberleek allegedly released the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior, sparking a race within the homebrew scene to port the build to PC. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.
But it looks like Take-Two is taking action, reportedly convincing GitHub to delete an entire network of 3,007 repositories via a DMCA takedown notice.
The takedown we know about relates to ItsNotRexed's GitHub repository and the over 2,900 forks attached to it, which Take-Two said facilitated copyright infringement of GTA 6. Take-Two alleged that the repository Project Leonida repository "exceeds the license Rockstar Games grants to users, constituting copyright infringement.” Here, Take-Two claimed that the repository violated at least Section 2.3 of Rockstar Games’ terms of service:
"The limited license granted in this Agreement does not give you any right to, and you may not, sell, copy, loan, lease, distribute, disassemble, decompile, decrypt, hack, derive source code from, reverse engineer, modify, create derivative works, commercialize, or otherwise exploit the Services (including the Content), Virtual Items, or your Account unless subject to separate, express written terms provided by Rockstar permitting such conduct.” Additionally, there’s an interesting note in the takedown order that addresses the “bring your own files” defence we’ve seen so often from the homebrew community when it comes to unofficial ports of video games. As you’d expect, Take-Two isn’t in favor of it, insisting that in this case, the files the user must provide come from the unauthorized GTA 6 Xbox build Cyberleek leaked online.
IGN has asked Take-Two for comment.
According to now deleted social media posts, NotRexed, author of the Leonida project, shut it down entirely. There are also screenshots of its Discord showing users posting disclaimers distancing themselves from Project Leonida in case of a federal investigation.
However, many similar projects remain active, risking similar action from Take-Two. Seemingly undeterred, these projects are ongoing, with some getting close to creating a PC port of GTA 6 that is somewhat playable. Some are even streaming their efforts, showing how they are vibecoding a port using agent prompts such as "make no mistakes," "keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," and "work faster."
This is of course a nightmare scenario for Take-Two and Sony and Microsoft, which are benefiting greatly from GTA 6 releasing on console only. The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. As a result, there is huge interest in a potential PC version offering 60fps gameplay.
As you've probably seen from various viral clips on social media, people are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. We've seen everything from Minecraft playable inside X/Twitter to modders crashing Minecraft and Elden Ring together . Indeed, last month, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline.
Seemingly in response, Anthropic issued an update for Claude that made it harder for people to use the AI model to generate video game clones. In an interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.
Some of this concern has to do with the security of the PS5, with Sony seemingly engaged in a game of Whac-a-Mole with hackers who are trying to jailbreak the latest firmware. If a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6 to run, it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and subsequently made available on PC.
Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.
Here’s the exchange:
IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?
Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.
IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games?

pool.titulo: Raul Bautista Actor Manny Perez Bought a PS5 So He Could Play GTA 6
pool.resumen: The actor behind one of the best GTA characters of all time has started working his way through GTA 6. Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista, bought a PS5 just so he could play.
pool.contenido:
The actor behind one of the best GTA characters of all time has started working his way through GTA 6 . Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista, bought a PS5 just so he could play.
“Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy!” he said in a video posted to social media . “Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.”
According to Perez, the biggest issue as a non-gamer has been getting used to the DualSense controller, which he called “the stick,” but he’s “getting there.”
The actor sent a follow-up tweet after a fan shared the video. “Will take a while but I will finish this game,” he said. “Thank you all for the support. I’m loving the comments and appreciations.”
Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow.
Raul Batista is a big character in GTA 6 from Chapter 3 onwards, and one of the highlights of the game in terms of performance. Batista steals the show in some really cool scenes, which I won’t spoil, but I can see him becoming a fan favorite as people work their way through the story.
Perez has also been touring Miami and recreating iconic scenes from GTA 6, including his in-car introduction from the Extended Look. Here’s a post showing some of the photos:
It’s kind of killing me how Raul Bautista’s actor (Manny Perez) is already out here touring Miami and recreating scenes from the game LMAO
I love this guy, GOAT @MannyPerez1 https://t.co/KyMhGco8su
— GameRoll (@GameRoll_) November 23, 2026
Perez isn't the only GTA 6 actor who's started to talk about their work on the game and fan reaction to their character. For example, Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online. And Issa Lopez, who plays a radio host on GTA 6’s fictional Cocoteo FM radio station, described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game , calling the project “crazy secretive.”

pool.titulo: Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus
pool.resumen:
At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason.

pool.resumen:
On September 9, 2026, at 3:35pm Pacific Time, SiegfriedX unlocked a 110-point XBOX Achievement that pushed his Gamerscore to a historic 10 million. The post Achievement Unlocked: An Interview with the First XBOX Player to Reach 10 Million Gamerscore appeared first on XBOX Wire .
pool.contenido:
On September 9, 2026, at 3:35pm Pacific Time, SiegfriedX unlocked a 110-point XBOX Achievement that pushed his Gamerscore to a historic 10 million. With that, he became the first XBOX player in the world to reach the milestone – just in time for XBOX’s 25th anniversary celebrations.
His journey began on XBOX 360, and it took 20 years and more than 6,400 games to get there. Along the way, he has racked up some remarkable accomplishments:
What Is Gamerscore?
Gamerscore is an individual scoring system introduced with the launch of XBOX 360 in 2005. It represents the achievement points a player has earned across XBOX games.
“Since 2020, so for the past six years, I’ve unlocked at least one achievement every day,” he told XBOX Wire Brazil in an exclusive interview.
SiegfriedX is the XBOX profile of Brazilian player Marcello Malta, a 42-year-old systems analyst whose biggest hobby is hunting achievements. “I like picking up a game and unlocking every achievement, even if the last one is worth just 10 points and takes 500 hours to get. I’m still going to try,” he says.
With a milestone like that, we wanted to hear more about his passion for achievements, how it all started, and what keeps him chasing that next unlock. Here’s what he had to say.
Achievements and Gamerscore were introduced with XBOX 360. What first got you interested in achievements?
Siegfried: I was hooked on achievements right away. I didn’t even know the system existed, and I don’t think it was something people really talked about at the time. It was just a feature built into the console. You certainly didn’t buy an XBOX knowing it was there, let alone knowing it would eventually influence the entire industry and inspire similar systems elsewhere.
I remember playing and suddenly seeing that notification pop up on the screen. I thought, “What is this?” So, I looked it up, found a couple of achievement websites, started learning how the system worked, and that was it. I was hooked.
Back then, achievements really encouraged you to experience everything a game had to offer: finish the campaign, beat it on the highest difficulty, find all the collectibles, and complete specific challenges along the way. To me, they felt like the developer’s vision for how they wanted you to experience the game. Almost like they were saying, “If you’ve done all of this, you’ve seen my entire game, from beginning to end, and everything I created for you.”
What Are Achievements?
Achievements are specific goals and objectives players can complete in a game to earn Gamerscore points. Examples: finishing it on hard difficulty, collecting every collectible, or defeating a set number of opponents in multiplayer.
Each game released on XBOX includes 1,000G worth of achievements to unlock. That total can increase with additional content and expansions.
What motivates you most when it comes to chasing an achievement?
Siegfried: I first fell in love with games through Nintendo, and their games have always had that focus on collecting things and completing everything. I think that mindset stuck with me from the very beginning. achievements became an extension of that, another way of going after everything a game has to offer.
I’ve never been interested in earning points just for the sake of earning points. When I start a game, I want to unlock every achievement, even if the last one is worth just 10 points and takes 500 hours to get. I’m still going to try. I might give up or not make it in the end, but I always start with the same goal: to get everything, no matter how much time or effort it takes.
You recently reached 10 million Gamerscore. How did you plan the achievement that would take you to that milestone?
Siegfried: I wanted to hit 10 million with a game that meant something to me, something I really loved and that could make the milestone feel even more special. So I decided to do it by completing the full 1,000G in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth .
Final Fantasy is a franchise I love, so it felt like the perfect choice. The final achievement I unlocked was for beating the game on its hardest difficulty. That completed the full achievement list and brought me to exactly 10 million Gamerscore.
Was being the first player to reach 10 million Gamerscore always a goal for you?
Siegfried: I never really had a specific goal in mind. Because of the way I play, always trying to complete everything, I naturally ended up second or third in the world for Gamerscore, with someone else usually ahead of me.
Over time, though, people started dropping out, either because they got tired of chasing achievements or simply decided they didn’t want to keep going. That left me at 9 million Gamerscore with a real shot at becoming the first person to reach 10 million. That’s when I really started pushing for it.
When XBOX 360 launched, the idea of anyone ever reaching 10 million Gamerscore was almost unthinkable. But I don’t have another milestone in mind now. For me, the goal has always been to play, have fun, and do what I enjoy.
“When I start a game, I see it through to the end, at least when it comes to the original achievement list. I’ve been doing that for more than 10 years.”
Looking back on your achievement journey, which one was the hardest to unlock?
Siegfried: For me difficulty comes down on how much time something takes. Some achievements can be incredibly time-consuming, and Monster Hunter: World is a great example.
Getting every gold crown in Monster Hunter: World for the Giant Crown Master achievement was one of the toughest things I’ve ever done. It can be really frustrating to play for one, two, or even three days without making any progress because so much of it comes down to luck and getting the right monsters appear. It makes you want to cry and give up. [Laughs]

pool.titulo: AI kills another coding competition: 'I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models'
pool.resumen: After eight years of operation, the Atari Homebrew Awards are no more.
pool.contenido:
The Atari Homebrew Awards , an annual celebration of new games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI.
"As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums .
"Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of new AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.
"The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the new fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I quickly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought."
James said he discovered last week that "a large majority" of developers were using AI in some capacity to make their games, from testing to wholesale game creation, "without one typed line of code." That left two options: Disallow any and all AI usage in the Atari Homebrew Awards competition, which James said would disqualify a large number of "extremely talented coders" who used AI in some very minor way, or let it slide and choose some sort of arbitrary dividing line between what is and isn't allowed—or just let it go entirely and allow everything, including fully vibe-coded games.
James said he wasn't interested in that, which meant he needed to settle on how much AI usage would be allowable—and also how to determine if AI was used at all, since some developers are better at disclosure than others. That, naturally, led to the worry that developers could be subject to "false positives and possible witch hunts," something that's already a problem in mainstream game development.
This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year.
ZeroPage Homebrew, Atari Homebrew Awards host
Ultimately, James decided there was no practical way forward, although he did leave open the possibility of a return someday. "This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year," he wrote. "I know many others feel the same way and I hope to be able to continue this tradition in the coming years as things settle into a new normal."
As we noted in July, debates over "acceptable" levels of AI use are cropping up all over the open source development scene : Some are drawing hard lines against it for principled and/or practical reasons, yet its popularity is growing explosively because, frankly, you don't need to know what you're doing in order to do it—as long as you're not too concerned with doing it well.
The Atari Homebrew Awards isn't the first such event to fall victim to the AI flood. Earlier in November, the Australian STEM Videogame Challenge, a "free national videogame development competition for students," announced that the 2026 event will be its last because "the rapid and complex rise of generative AI in game development [made] it harder to judge what students made themselves," and thus undercut the whole purpose of the program: Encouraging kids to learn how to code.

pool.titulo: Someone counted all 5,588 buildings in GTA 6, and it turns out you can go inside 28% of them
pool.resumen: Maybe even more will open up for Online, too.
pool.contenido:
Grand Theft Auto 6 hasn't even been out for a week yet, and someone has already done the math on how many buildings in the whole of Leonida you can actually walk into. For those of you who are curious: it's 1,563 buildings.
That is frankly ridiculous. I don't think I've ever been inside 1,563 different buildings in my entire life, although I am a creature of habit, so that could explain things. The player who shared these stats, Aileos , does note that there are 5,588 buildings in total, so the enterable buildings only account for a fraction of that, just over 25%.
There are some who will look at this with a glass-half-empty perspective, and I get it. This world is so cool, it's easy to want more of it, but as another player points out , "This would've sent us into psychosis a few years back". Sometimes it's better to focus on what we have rather than what we don't have. After all, how many buildings will you realistically enter in your GTA 6 playthrough? Probably not 1,563.
We've spent the past week here in the PC Gamer Slack channel marvelling at just how many random encounters you can stumble across in GTA 6. Some of us have found sentient NPCs. One of us was actually recognised by a convenience store clerk who then asked to get robbed, and I think we've all seen videos of the furry rescue mission.
But just because this world already has loads of awesome activities, it doesn't mean we aren't hoping for more. A massive casino and go-kart track have been spotted by players, both of which have huge "Coming Soon" signs draped outside of them.
These buildings could be lying in wait for GTA 6 Online, or they could be added to singleplayer sometime in the future. Regardless, those are two more buildings that will potentially welcome players soon.

pool.titulo: How to steal the Pegassi Infernus in GTA 6
pool.resumen: Pilfer the '96 Infernus from the police lockup for Randy.
pool.contenido:
Stealing the Pegassi Infernus in GTA 6 can be quite tricky, considering it's being held in the police department lockup, the building to the west of the police station in southwest Crosstown.
You can access the building via a yellow window cleaning elevator on the southern side of the building. But this won't appear until Randy texts and gives you the Infernus's location. If you go here before, your options for entering are far more limited and risky, so it's worth waiting. To get to the car:
Use the elevator to get inside. Turn right, then left, and make your way up to the seventh level of the multi-story car park—the purple Pegassi Infernus is easy to recognise since it's the only sports car in there. Select the key cloning option to get inside. Now you just need to drive down a few levels to exit via the police station parking lot—which I'd recommend—or keep going all the way down to exit at the bottom of the car park. Remember, you need to drive fast to stop the tracker going off, and if you hear it beeping, you should speed up to prevent it pinging the cops.
If you do bash around the car a bit, you can get it repaired at a gas station on the way. Bring it back in pristine condition and you'll net 15k for the trouble.
